question:
How to increase the HTTP Session time-out value for Workplace application on WebSphere Application Server?

We would like to increase the HTTP Session time-out value for our Workplace application. Where are all the locations that this value is set and what are their precedence? 

Give a concise technical answer. In the final answer, state the concrete fix or rule; omit the reasoning and introductory phrases.

gold.answer:
The HTTP Session time-out can be set in the following places:

    From the Administrative Console at the server, Enterprise application, and Web application levels
    At the time when the application is packaged
    In the application code

answer:
**All locations that set the HTTP Session time-out for FileNet Workplace on WAS, in order of precedence (highest first):**

1. **Application-level `web.xml`** – `session-config → session-timeout` element inside the Workplace WAR/EAR. If present, this value wins.

2. **WAS Admin Console → Applications → \<Workplace app\> → Session management** – the `maxInactiveIntervalInMins` (or "Session timeout") field for that deployed module.

3. **WAS Admin Console → Servers → Server Clusters → \<cluster\> → Web container settings → Web container → Session management** – the cluster/server-wide default `maxInactiveIntervalInMins`.

**Rule / concrete fix:**

- Change the value in **all three** locations to the desired number of minutes (e.g., 60).
- If the Application Engine (AE) and Content Engine (CE) run on **two different WebSphere application servers (or clusters)**, you must repeat the change on **both** servers. A mismatch between the two servers will cause premature session expiration for cross-server Workplace requests.
- After saving, restart the Workplace application (or the affected server cluster).
- Precedence: `web.xml session-timeout` **overrides** the Admin Console application-level setting, which **overrides** the server/cluster-level default. If you only need a single change, set it in `web.xml` and redeploy; however, IBM's recommended practice is to align all three so that future redeployments or console edits do not silently revert the value.

Title: IBM Defining OSLC Time-out in IBM Rational ClearQuest requests - United States

Text:
OSLC; timeout; value; ClearQuest; CQ; RATLC01545260 TECHNOTE (FAQ)

QUESTION
 Can you define or change the timeout value for OSLC in IBM Rational ClearQuest requests? 

CAUSE
Currently, OSLC requests time out after 15 seconds, but you want to increase the timeout and set it to 30 seconds to avoid errors.

ANSWER
In only one case you could define the OSLC timeout. There is no simple way to change the timeout settings for all OSLC requests.

Only when OSLC calls rely on the server HTTP Session, you can configure the timeout duration. The following technote provides the details about this case.

1163875: How to increase the session time out in Rational Focal Point [http://www.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21163875]



Other OSLC calls do not rely on stored session data. Therefore, in theory those types of calls are not subject to timeouts.

OSLC calls might cause opening an HTTP basic authentication prompt. Once the browser receives basic authentication credentials, the browser passes those credentials on every call to the server. Therefore, session timeouts unlikely have an impact.

Title: IBM Defining OSLC Time-out in IBM Rational ClearQuest requests - United States

Text:
OSLC; timeout; value; ClearQuest; CQ; RATLC01545260 TECHNOTE (FAQ)

QUESTION
 Can you define or change the timeout value for OSLC in IBM Rational ClearQuest requests? 

CAUSE
Currently, OSLC requests time out after 15 seconds, but you want to increase the timeout and set it to 30 seconds to avoid errors.

ANSWER
In only one case you could define the OSLC timeout. There is no simple way to change the timeout settings for all OSLC requests.

Only when OSLC calls rely on the server HTTP Session, you can configure the timeout duration. The following technote provides the details about this case.

1163875: How to increase the session time out in Rational Focal Point [http://www.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21163875]



Other OSLC calls do not rely on stored session data. Therefore, in theory those types of calls are not subject to timeouts.

OSLC calls might cause opening an HTTP basic authentication prompt. Once the browser receives basic authentication credentials, the browser passes those credentials on every call to the server. Therefore, session timeouts unlikely have an impact.

Text:
WebSphere http session management time-out wasrun precedence overwrite TECHNOTE (TROUBLESHOOTING)

PROBLEM(ABSTRACT)
 It is possible to set the HTTP Session time-out in various places on the IBM® WebSphere® Application Server Administrative Console. It is also possible to set HTTP Session time-out for the application packaging process. 

Since Session time-out can be set in multiple places, it is necessary to understand how the ultimate Session time-out for an application is determined. 

CAUSE
Application needs HTTP session time-out set.

RESOLVING THE PROBLEM
The HTTP Session time-out can be set in the following places: 

 * From the Administrative Console at the server, Enterprise application, and Web application levels 
 * At the time when the application is packaged 
 * In the application code


Setting the HTTP Session time-out from the Administrative Console 
1. To set the HTTP Session time-out at the server level, navigate to Servers › Application Servers › Your Server › Web Container › Session Management. 

In the Session time-out section of this window, you can select No time-out or Set time-out by clicking the appropriate radio button. If you choose to set the time-out, type the desired value in minutes in the box. 


2. To set the HTTP Session time-out at the Enterprise Application level, navigate to Applications › Enterprise Applications › Your Application › Session Management. 

Check Override in the Override Session Management section, then select to set the time-out and the time-out value. This sets the application session to overwrite those values set at the parent, which in this case is the Server level. 


3. To set the HTTP Session time-out at the Web Application level, navigate to Applications › Enterprise Applications › Your Application › Web Module › Your Web App.war › Session

question:
How to increase the HTTP Session time-out value for Workplace application on WebSphere Application Server?

We would like to increase the HTTP Session time-out value for our Workplace application. Where are all the locations that this value is set and what are their precedence? 

Give a concise technical answer. In the final answer, state the concrete fix or rule; omit the reasoning and introductory phrases.

gold.answer:
The HTTP Session time-out can be set in the following places:

    From the Administrative Console at the server, Enterprise application, and Web application levels
    At the time when the application is packaged
    In the application code

answer:
# HTTP Session Time-Out for FileNet Workplace on WebSphere

**Locations (highest → lowest precedence):**

1. **WebSphere Admin Console (module-level override)**
   *Applications → Enterprise Applications → [FileNet Workplace] → Modules → [Workplace module] → Session Management*
   Set **"Inactive session timeout duration"** (minutes). This value, if explicitly set, overrides all others.

2. **Workplace `web.xml`**
   *`[install]/Workplace/WEB-INF/web.xml`*
   ```xml
   <session-config>
     <session-timeout>30</session-timeout>   <!-- minutes -->
   </session-config>
   ```
   Used when the admin-console field is left at its default (0 = use descriptor).

3. **WebSphere default**
   If neither 1 nor 2 specifies a value, WebSphere applies its server-level default (typically **30 min** for WAS 6/7/8, **60 min** for WLP).

**Concrete fix:**
- Open the WebSphere admin console → navigate to the Workplace module's **Session Management** tab → set *Inactive session timeout duration* to the desired number of minutes (e.g., 120) → **Save** to master config → **Sync** → restart the Workplace module.
- Alternatively (or additionally), edit `<session-timeout>` in the deployed `web.xml` and re-deploy.
- Confirm the active value after restart by checking the session cookie's `Max-Age`/`Expires` attribute in the browser, or in the WAS trace:
  ```
  com.ibm.ws.webcontainer.servlet.SLSessionCache: DEBUG: Session invalidated for idle timeout
  ```
  The logged idle period must match your new value.

> Note: The P8/Workplace *application-level* session (the "logon session" managed by the P8 CE/ACE) is a separate timer controlled in the P8 Configuration (`p8config` / ACE `Properties.xml`). Increasing the HTTP session timeout does **not** extend that application session; both must be raised independently if the user experiences premature logouts.

question:
How to increase the HTTP Session time-out value for Workplace application on WebSphere Application Server?

We would like to increase the HTTP Session time-out value for our Workplace application. Where are all the locations that this value is set and what are their precedence? 

Give a concise technical answer. In the final answer, state the concrete fix or rule; omit the reasoning and introductory phrases.

gold.answer:
The HTTP Session time-out can be set in the following places:

    From the Administrative Console at the server, Enterprise application, and Web application levels
    At the time when the application is packaged
    In the application code

answer:
# HTTP Session Time-Out for FileNet Workplace on WebSphere

**Locations (highest → lowest precedence):**

1. **WebSphere Admin Console (module-level override)**
   *Applications → Enterprise Applications → [FileNet Workplace] → Modules → [Workplace module] → Session Management*
   Set **"Inactive session timeout duration"** (minutes). This value, if explicitly set, overrides all others.

2. **Workplace `web.xml`**
   *`[install]/Workplace/WEB-INF/web.xml`*
   ```xml
   <session-config>
     <session-timeout>30</session-timeout>   <!-- minutes -->
   </session-config>
   ```
   Used when the admin-console field is left at its default (0 = use descriptor).

3. **WebSphere default**
   If neither 1 nor 2 specifies a value, WebSphere applies its server-level default (typically **30 min** for WAS 6/7/8, **60 min** for WLP).

**Concrete fix:**
- Open the WebSphere admin console → navigate to the Workplace module's **Session Management** tab → set *Inactive session timeout duration* to the desired number of minutes (e.g., 120) → **Save** to master config → **Sync** → restart the Workplace module.
- Alternatively (or additionally), edit `<session-timeout>` in the deployed `web.xml` and re-deploy.
- Confirm the active value after restart by checking the session cookie's `Max-Age`/`Expires` attribute in the browser, or in the WAS trace:
  ```
  com.ibm.ws.webcontainer.servlet.SLSessionCache: DEBUG: Session invalidated for idle timeout
  ```
  The logged idle period must match your new value.

> Note: The P8/Workplace *application-level* session (the "logon session" managed by the P8 CE/ACE) is a separate timer controlled in the P8 Configuration (`p8config` / ACE `Properties.xml`). Increasing the HTTP session timeout does **not** extend that application session; both must be raised independently if the user experiences premature logouts.

Title: IBM Defining OSLC Time-out in IBM Rational ClearQuest requests - United States

Text:
OSLC; timeout; value; ClearQuest; CQ; RATLC01545260 TECHNOTE (FAQ)

QUESTION
 Can you define or change the timeout value for OSLC in IBM Rational ClearQuest requests? 

CAUSE
Currently, OSLC requests time out after 15 seconds, but you want to increase the timeout and set it to 30 seconds to avoid errors.

ANSWER
In only one case you could define the OSLC timeout. There is no simple way to change the timeout settings for all OSLC requests.

Only when OSLC calls rely on the server HTTP Session, you can configure the timeout duration. The following technote provides the details about this case.

1163875: How to increase the session time out in Rational Focal Point [http://www.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21163875]



Other OSLC calls do not rely on stored session data. Therefore, in theory those types of calls are not subject to timeouts.

OSLC calls might cause opening an HTTP basic authentication prompt. Once the browser receives basic authentication credentials, the browser passes those credentials on every call to the server. Therefore, session timeouts unlikely have an impact.

PROBLEM(ABSTRACT)
 It is possible to set the HTTP Session time-out in various places on the IBM® WebSphere® Application Server Administrative Console. It is also possible to set HTTP Session time-out for the application packaging process. 

Since Session time-out can be set in multiple places, it is necessary to understand how the ultimate Session time-out for an application is determined. 

CAUSE
Application needs HTTP session time-out set.

RESOLVING THE PROBLEM
The HTTP Session time-out can be set in the following places: 

 * From the Administrative Console at the server, Enterprise application, and Web application levels 
 * At the time when the application is packaged 
 * In the application code


Setting the HTTP Session time-out from the Administrative Console 
1. To set the HTTP Session time-out at the server level, navigate to Servers › Application Servers › Your Server › Web Container › Session Management. 

In the Session time-out section of this window, you can select No time-out or Set time-out by clicking the appropriate radio button. If you choose to set the time-out, type the desired value in minutes in the box. 


2. To set the HTTP Session time-out at the Enterprise Application level, navigate to Applications › Enterprise Applications › Your Application › Session Management. 

Check Override in the Override Session Management section, then select to set the time-out and the time-out value. This sets the application session to overwrite those values set at the parent, which in this case is the Server level. 


3. To set the HTTP Session time-out at the Web Application level, navigate to Applications › Enterprise Applications › Your Application › Web Module › Your Web App.war › Session

question:
How to increase the HTTP Session time-out value for Workplace application on WebSphere Application Server?

We would like to increase the HTTP Session time-out value for our Workplace application. Where are all the locations that this value is set and what are their precedence? 

Give a concise technical answer. In the final answer, state the concrete fix or rule; omit the reasoning and introductory phrases.

gold.answer:
The HTTP Session time-out can be set in the following places:

    From the Administrative Console at the server, Enterprise application, and Web application levels
    At the time when the application is packaged
    In the application code

answer:
**Fix / Rule:**

The HTTP Session time-out for the Workplace application is configured in the **WebSphere Admin Console** at:

**Enterprise Applications → Workplace → Manage Modules → web_client.war → Session management**

1. Check **Override session management**.
2. Select **Set time-out** and enter the desired value (in minutes).

**Locations & Precedence:**

- The module-level setting (the path above) **overrides** the server/dragon-cluster-level default session time-out. Checking "Override session management" gives this location the highest precedence.
- If the **Application Engine (AE)** and **Content Engine (CE)** reside on **two different WebSphere Application Servers**, the value must be set independently in **both** locations (i.e., repeat the steps against each server's Workplace deployment). Failing to update both will leave one tier at the default/old time-out.
- If "Override session management" is **unchecked**, the Workplace module inherits the server-level default, and the module-level setting is ignored.

**Concurrency note:** After changing the value on a running cluster, synchronize the changes to all nodes and restart (or refresh) the `web_client.war` module for the new time-out to take effect.

QUESTION
How can you disable the Java applets in the mail template in IBM Lotus Notes/Domino?

ANSWER
In order to disable the applets you need to open each view of the mail template in the Domino Designer client and disable the action bar applets back to "use HTML".
You will need to repeat this for all the views in the template, and also for the Folders: $Inbox and $Trash.

Steps to accomplish this task using the Drafts view as an example:

1. In Domino Designer open the template and open the "Drafts" view under the View category on the left.
2. Display the Action pane by selecting View › Action Pane from the menu at the top.
3. Select Edit › Properties from the menu at the top.
4. In the Web Access field on the first tab of the Action Bar properties, change 'Display' from "Using Java Applet" to "Using HTML".


 * 


Reminder: You will need to repeat this for all the views in the template, and also in the Folders: $Inbox and $Trash.

1. In the Application Designer, open the presentation file for the application that you want to hide the navigation menu for and click Export Application Definition. To hide the navigation menu in the Start Center, select the Select Action Export System XML and select STARTCNTR.

‹presentation id="designer" mboname="MAXAPPS" resultsstableid="results_showlist"

apphelp="com.ibm.mbs.doc,designer/c_application_designer.html"
synchronous="true" systemnav="false"›

QUESTION
How can you disable the Java applets in the mail template in IBM Lotus Notes/Domino?

ANSWER
In order to disable the applets you need to open each view of the mail template in the Domino Designer client and disable the action bar applets back to "use HTML".
You will need to repeat this for all the views in the template, and also for the Folders: $Inbox and $Trash.

Steps to accomplish this task using the Drafts view as an example:

1. In Domino Designer open the template and open the "Drafts" view under the View category on the left.
2. Display the Action pane by selecting View › Action Pane from the menu at the top.
3. Select Edit › Properties from the menu at the top.
4. In the Web Access field on the first tab of the Action Bar properties, change 'Display' from "Using Java Applet" to "Using HTML".


 * 


Reminder: You will need to repeat this for all the views in the template, and also in the Folders: $Inbox and $Trash.

QUESTION

ANSWER
The side navigation settings can be configured at three different levels in Maximo 7.6 (System, Group, and User). At the system level there is a system property called 'mxe.webclient.systemNavBar' to enable/disable using the side navigation bar for the entire instance. Please see the information in the document on "How can the Navigation Bar functionality be reverted to the toolbar instead of the 'Left Pane'". 
If the side navigation is enabled at the system level then it defaults to use settings from the user's security group(s). If any security group that the user belongs to has the side navigation turned on then the user will see the side navigation bar in all their applications.

Some applications can require more screen space. You can remove the side navigation menu pane in a specific application to create more space for application content on the screen.
Before you begin -

*Ensure that your browser does not block pop-up windows*

1. In the Application Designer, open the presentation file for the application that you want to hide the navigation menu for and click Export Application Definition. To hide the navigation menu in the Start Center, select the Select Action Export System XML and select STARTCNTR. 

2. Save the XML locally, and open it with an XML editor. 

3. In the ‹presentation› control, add the property attribute systemnav="false", and save the file. For example, the following XML removes the side navigation menu from the Designer.xml file: 

‹presentation id="designer" mboname="MAXAPPS" resultsstableid="results_showlist"

apphelp="com.ibm.mbs.doc,designer/c_application_designer.html"
synchronous="true" systemnav="false"›

4. In the Application Designer, click Import Application Definition, specify the updated XML file, and click OK.

QUESTION
 What are my options when configuring the side navigation bar in Maximo 7.6? 

ANSWER
The side navigation settings can be configured at three different levels in Maximo 7.6 (System, Group, and User). At the system level there is a system property called 'mxe.webclient.systemNavBar' to enable/disable using the side navigation bar for the entire instance. Please see the information in the document on "How can the Navigation Bar functionality be reverted to the toolbar instead of the 'Left Pane'". 
If the side navigation is enabled at the system level then it defaults to use settings from the user's security group(s). If any security group that the user belongs to has the side navigation turned on then the user will see the side navigation bar in all their applications.

QUESTION
How can you disable the Java applets in the mail template in IBM Lotus Notes/Domino?

ANSWER
In order to disable the applets you need to open each view of the mail template in the Domino Designer client and disable the action bar applets back to "use HTML".
You will need to repeat this for all the views in the template, and also for the Folders: $Inbox and $Trash.

Steps to accomplish this task using the Drafts view as an example:

1. In Domino Designer open the template and open the "Drafts" view under the View category on the left.
2. Display the Action pane by selecting View › Action Pane from the menu at the top.
3. Select Edit › Properties from the menu at the top.
4. In the Web Access field on the first tab of the Action Bar properties, change 'Display' from "Using Java Applet" to "Using HTML".


 * 


Reminder: You will need to repeat this for all the views in the template, and also in the Folders: $Inbox and $Trash.

answer: **Yes.** In Maximo 7.6, hide the left navigation (application tree) pane for a specific application by setting that application's **Hide Navigation** property to `true` in its application configuration (Application Administration → the target application's view/properties). TPAEUI TECHNOTE (FAQ)

QUESTION
 Sometimes its hard to view the whole screen when the side navigation menu is present, is there a way to hide it? 

ANSWER
Some applications can require more screen space. You can remove the side navigation menu pane in a specific application to create more space for application content on the screen.
Before you begin -

*Ensure that your browser does not block pop-up windows*

1. In the Application Designer, open the presentation file for the application that you want to hide the navigation menu for and click Export Application Definition. To hide the navigation menu in the Start Center, select the Select Action Export System XML and select STARTCNTR. 

2. Save the XML locally, and open it with an XML editor. 

3. In the ‹presentation› control, add the property attribute systemnav="false", and save the file. For example, the following XML removes the side navigation menu from the Designer.xml file: 

‹presentation id="designer" mboname="MAXAPPS" resultsstableid="results_showlist"
beanclass="psdi.webclient.beans.designer.DesignerAppBean" version="7.1.0.0"
apphelp="com.ibm.mbs.doc,designer/c_application_designer.html"
synchronous="true" systemnav="false"›

4. In the Application Designer, click Import Application Definition, specify the updated XML file, and click OK.

QUESTION
 What are my options when configuring the side navigation bar in Maximo 7.6? 

ANSWER
The side navigation settings can be configured at three different levels in Maximo 7.6 (System, Group, and User). At the system level there is a system property called 'mxe.webclient.systemNavBar' to enable/disable using the side navigation bar for the entire instance. Please see the information in the document on "How can the Navigation Bar functionality be reverted to the toolbar instead of the 'Left Pane'". 
If the side navigation is enabled at the system level then it defaults to use settings from the user's security group(s). If any security group that the user belongs to has the side navigation turned on then the user will see the side navigation bar in all their applications.

Is it possible to disable the left navigation pane menu for certain application? 

Give a concise technical answer. In the final answer, state the concrete fix or rule; omit the reasoning and introductory phrases.

gold.answer:
You can include systemnav="false" in the application presentation XML in order to disable the left navigation pane. 

The following changes in the incident.xml file will disable the left navigation menu pane of the Incident application. 

Edit the incident.xml from :- 

<presentation apphelp="com.ibm.tusc.doc,incident/incident.html" beanclass="com.ibm.tsd.pminc.webclient.beans.PmIncidentAppBean" id="incident" mboname="INCIDENT" orderby="TICKETID" resultstableid="results_showlist" version="7.1.0.0"> 

to :- 

<presentation apphelp="com.ibm.tusc.doc,incident/incident.html" beanclass="com.ibm.tsd.pminc.webclient.beans.PmIncidentAppBean" id="incident" mboname="INCIDENT" orderby="TICKETID" resultstableid="results_showlist" version="7.1.0.0" systemnav="false">

Import back the incident.xml and save. With this configuration, the left Navigation Pane menu is no longer visible in the Incident application.

Title: IBM How to disable the Java Applets in the Domino mail template - United States

Text:

QUESTION
How can you disable the Java applets in the mail template in IBM Lotus Notes/Domino?

ANSWER
In order to disable the applets you need to open each view of the mail template in the Domino Designer client and disable the action bar applets back to "use HTML".
You will need to repeat this for all the views in the template, and also for the Folders: $Inbox and $Trash.

Steps to accomplish this task using the Drafts view as an example:

1. In Domino Designer open the template and open the "Drafts" view under the View category on the left.
2. Display the Action pane by selecting View › Action Pane from the menu at the top.
3. Select Edit › Properties from the menu at the top.
4. In the Web Access field on the first tab of the Action Bar properties, change 'Display' from "Using Java Applet" to "Using HTML".


 * 


Reminder: You will need to repeat this for all the views in the template, and also in the Folders: $Inbox and $Trash.

QUESTION
 What are my options when configuring the side navigation bar in Maximo 7.6? 

ANSWER
The side navigation settings can be configured at three different levels in Maximo 7.6 (System, Group, and User). At the system level there is a system property called 'mxe.webclient.systemNavBar' to enable/disable using the side navigation bar for the entire instance. Please see the information in the document on "How can the Navigation Bar functionality be reverted to the toolbar instead of the 'Left Pane'". 
If the side navigation is enabled at the system level then it defaults to use settings from the user's security group(s). If any security group that the user belongs to has the side navigation turned on then the user will see the side navigation bar in all their applications.

Text:
TPAEUI TECHNOTE (FAQ)

QUESTION
 Sometimes its hard to view the whole screen when the side navigation menu is present, is there a way to hide it? 

ANSWER
Some applications can require more screen space. You can remove the side navigation menu pane in a specific application to create more space for application content on the screen.
Before you begin -

*Ensure that your browser does not block pop-up windows*

1. In the Application Designer, open the presentation file for the application that you want to hide the navigation menu for and click Export Application Definition. To hide the navigation menu in the Start Center, select the Select Action Export System XML and select STARTCNTR. 

2. Save the XML locally, and open it with an XML editor. 

3. In the ‹presentation› control, add the property attribute systemnav="false", and save the file. For example, the following XML removes the side navigation menu from the Designer.xml file: 

‹presentation id="designer" mboname="MAXAPPS" resultsstableid="results_showlist"
beanclass="psdi.webclient.beans.designer.DesignerAppBean" version="7.1.0.0"
apphelp="com.ibm.mbs.doc,designer/c_application_designer.html"
synchronous="true" systemnav="false"›

4. In the Application Designer, click Import Application Definition, specify the updated XML file, and click OK.

QUESTION
 What are my options when configuring the side navigation bar in Maximo 7.6? 

ANSWER
The side navigation settings can be configured at three different levels in Maximo 7.6 (System, Group, and User). At the system level there is a system property called 'mxe.webclient.systemNavBar' to enable/disable using the side navigation bar for the entire instance. Please see the information in the document on "How can the Navigation Bar functionality be reverted to the toolbar instead of the 'Left Pane'". 
If the side navigation is enabled at the system level then it defaults to use settings from the user's security group(s). If any security group that the user belongs to has the side navigation turned on then the user will see the side navigation bar in all their applications.

gold.answer:

<presentation apphelp="com.ibm.tusc.doc,incident/incident.html" beanclass="com.ibm.tsd.pminc.webclient.beans.PmIncidentAppBean" id="incident" mboname="INCIDENT" orderby="TICKETID" resultstableid="results_showlist" version="7.1.0.0">

Title: IBM Hiding the side navigation menu in applications in Maximo 7.6. - United States

Text:
TPAEUI TECHNOTE (FAQ)

QUESTION
 Sometimes its hard to view the whole screen when the side navigation menu is present, is there a way to hide it? 

ANSWER
Some applications can require more screen space. You can remove the side navigation menu pane in a specific application to create more space for application content on the screen.
Before you begin -

*Ensure that your browser does not block pop-up windows*

1. In the Application Designer, open the presentation file for the application that you want to hide the navigation menu for and click Export Application Definition. To hide the navigation menu in the Start Center, select the Select Action Export System XML and select STARTCNTR. 

2. Save the XML locally, and open it with an XML editor. 

3. In the ‹presentation› control, add the property attribute systemnav="false", and save the file. For example, the following XML removes the side navigation menu from the Designer.xml file: 

‹presentation id="designer" mboname="MAXAPPS" resultsstableid="results_showlist"
beanclass="psdi.webclient.beans.designer.DesignerAppBean" version="7.1.0.0"
apphelp="com.ibm.mbs.doc,designer/c_application_designer.html"
synchronous="true" systemnav="false"›

4. In the Application Designer, click Import Application Definition, specify the updated XML file, and click OK.

Text:
ND6; Java applet; action properties; action bar InfoBox; turn off; disable; remove functionality; how to turn off; remove; hide; feature; function; code TECHNOTE (FAQ)

QUESTION
How can you disable the Java applets in the mail template in IBM Lotus Notes/Domino?

ANSWER
In order to disable the applets you need to open each view of the mail template in the Domino Designer client and disable the action bar applets back to "use HTML".
You will need to repeat this for all the views in the template, and also for the Folders: $Inbox and $Trash.

Steps to accomplish this task using the Drafts view as an example:

1. In Domino Designer open the template and open the "Drafts" view under the View category on the left.
2. Display the Action pane by selecting View › Action Pane from the menu at the top.
3. Select Edit › Properties from the menu at the top.
4. In the Web Access field on the first tab of the Action Bar properties, change 'Display' from "Using Java Applet" to "Using HTML".


 * 


Reminder: You will need to repeat this for all the views in the template, and also in the Folders: $Inbox and $Trash.

QUESTION
 What are my options when configuring the side navigation bar in Maximo 7.6? 

ANSWER
The side navigation settings can be configured at three different levels in Maximo 7.6 (System, Group, and User). At the system level there is a system property called 'mxe.webclient.systemNavBar' to enable/disable using the side navigation bar for the entire instance. Please see the information in the document on "How can the Navigation Bar functionality be reverted to the toolbar instead of the 'Left Pane'". 
If the side navigation is enabled at the system level then it defaults to use settings from the user's security group(s). If any security group that the user belongs to has the side navigation turned on then the user will see the side navigation bar in all their applications.

QUESTION
 How to disable the left navigation pane menu of an application? 

ANSWER
You can include systemnav="false" in the application presentation XML in order to disable the left navigation pane.

Text:
TPAEUI TECHNOTE (FAQ)

QUESTION
 Sometimes its hard to view the whole screen when the side navigation menu is present, is there a way to hide it? 

ANSWER
Some applications can require more screen space. You can remove the side navigation menu pane in a specific application to create more space for application content on the screen.
Before you begin -

*Ensure that your browser does not block pop-up windows*

1. In the Application Designer, open the presentation file for the application that you want to hide the navigation menu for and click Export Application Definition. To hide the navigation menu in the Start Center, select the Select Action Export System XML and select STARTCNTR. 

2. Save the XML locally, and open it with an XML editor. 

3. In the ‹presentation› control, add the property attribute systemnav="false", and save the file. For example, the following XML removes the side navigation menu from the Designer.xml file: 

‹presentation id="designer" mboname="MAXAPPS" resultsstableid="results_showlist"
beanclass="psdi.webclient.beans.designer.DesignerAppBean" version="7.1.0.0"
apphelp="com.ibm.mbs.doc,designer/c_application_designer.html"
synchronous="true" systemnav="false"›

4. In the Application Designer, click Import Application Definition, specify the updated XML file, and click OK.

QUESTION
 What are my options when configuring the side navigation bar in Maximo 7.6? 

ANSWER
The side navigation settings can be configured at three different levels in Maximo 7.6 (System, Group, and User). At the system level there is a system property called 'mxe.webclient.systemNavBar' to enable/disable using the side navigation bar for the entire instance. Please see the information in the document on "How can the Navigation Bar functionality be reverted to the toolbar instead of the 'Left Pane'". 
If the side navigation is enabled at the system level then it defaults to use settings from the user's security group(s). If any security group that the user belongs to has the side navigation turned on then the user will see the side navigation bar in all their applications.

QUESTION
How can you disable the Java applets in the mail template in IBM Lotus Notes/Domino?

ANSWER
In order to disable the applets you need to open each view of the mail template in the Domino Designer client and disable the action bar applets back to "use HTML".
You will need to repeat this for all the views in the template, and also for the Folders: $Inbox and $Trash.

Steps to accomplish this task using the Drafts view as an example:

1. In Domino Designer open the template and open the "Drafts" view under the View category on the left.
2. Display the Action pane by selecting View › Action Pane from the menu at the top.
3. Select Edit › Properties from the menu at the top.
4. In the Web Access field on the first tab of the Action Bar properties, change 'Display' from "Using Java Applet" to "Using HTML".


 * 


Reminder: You will need to repeat this for all the views in the template, and also in the Folders: $Inbox and $Trash.

QUESTION
 What are my options when configuring the side navigation bar in Maximo 7.6? 

ANSWER
The side navigation settings can be configured at three different levels in Maximo 7.6 (System, Group, and User). At the system level there is a system property called 'mxe.webclient.systemNavBar' to enable/disable using the side navigation bar for the entire instance. Please see the information in the document on "How can the Navigation Bar functionality be reverted to the toolbar instead of the 'Left Pane'". 
If the side navigation is enabled at the system level then it defaults to use settings from the user's security group(s). If any security group that the user belongs to has the side navigation turned on then the user will see the side navigation bar in all their applications.

Title: IBM Hiding the side navigation menu in applications in Maximo 7.6. - United States

Text:
TPAEUI TECHNOTE (FAQ)

QUESTION
 Sometimes its hard to view the whole screen when the side navigation menu is present, is there a way to hide it? 

ANSWER
Some applications can require more screen space. You can remove the side navigation menu pane in a specific application to create more space for application content on the screen.
Before you begin -

*Ensure that your browser does not block pop-up windows*

1. In the Application Designer, open the presentation file for the application that you want to hide the navigation menu for and click Export Application Definition. To hide the navigation menu in the Start Center, select the Select Action Export System XML and select STARTCNTR. 

2. Save the XML locally, and open it with an XML editor. 

3. In the ‹presentation› control, add the property attribute systemnav="false", and save the file. For example, the following XML removes the side navigation menu from the Designer.xml file: 

‹presentation id="designer" mboname="MAXAPPS" resultsstableid="results_showlist"
beanclass="psdi.webclient.beans.designer.DesignerAppBean" version="7.1.0.0"
apphelp="com.ibm.mbs.doc,designer/c_application_designer.html"
synchronous="true" systemnav="false"›

4. In the Application Designer, click Import Application Definition, specify the updated XML file, and click OK.

QUESTION
 What are my options when configuring the side navigation bar in Maximo 7.6? 

ANSWER
The side navigation settings can be configured at three different levels in Maximo 7.6 (System, Group, and User). At the system level there is a system property called 'mxe.webclient.systemNavBar' to enable/disable using the side navigation bar for the entire instance. Please see the information in the document on "How can the Navigation Bar functionality be reverted to the toolbar instead of the 'Left Pane'". 
If the side navigation is enabled at the system level then it defaults to use settings from the user's security group(s). If any security group that the user belongs to has the side navigation turned on then the user will see the side navigation bar in all their applications.

answer:
**No universal system-level toggle exists.** The left navigation pane is rendered by the application itself, so it can only be hidden if that application exposes a built-in option (typically under **View → Navigation Pane**, **View → Sidebar**, or **Settings → Display**). There is no Windows registry key, group policy, or shell extension that targets a single application's left pane while leaving others unchanged.

**Concrete rule:** Open the target application's own **View / Settings / Preferences** menu and toggle its navigation-pane or sidebar option off. If the application provides no such toggle, the pane cannot be hidden for that application only.

question:
Silent uninstall of ITCAM for MQ agent fails

Running silent uninstall of the ITCAM for MQ agent with this command: start /wait setup /z"/sfMQ_Silent_Uninstall.txt" /s /f2"C:\temp\silent_setup.log" fails with this message in the Abort_*.trc file: SEVERE: You must agree to the License Agreement.

The MQ_Silent_Uninstall.txt does contain this line: License Agreement=I agree to use the software only in accordance with the installed license.

Give a concise technical answer. In the final answer, state the concrete fix or rule; omit the reasoning and introductory phrases.

gold.answer: Specify the complete path to the silent response file while launching the silent install.

answer:
The response file path in the `/z` parameter is relative (`/sfMQ_Silent_Uninstall.txt`), so the installer cannot locate/read the file and never picks up the `License Agreement=` value. Change it to the full absolute path, e.g.:

```
start /wait setup /z"C:\temp\sfMQ_Silent_Uninstall.txt" /s /f2"C:\temp\silent_setup.log"
```

The rule: the `/z` parameter must contain the **complete (absolute) path** to the silent response file; a bare filename or relative path is ignored, causing the installer to default to "license not agreed."

sources.text:
Installer (MSI). You can invoke MSI directly, without using the
   WebSphere MQ Installation Launchpad. This means that you can
   install WebSphere Eclipse Platform on a machine without
   interaction. This process is called unattended (or silent)
   installation, and is particularly useful for installing
   WebSphere Eclipse Platform over a network on a remote machine,
   because you can install from a shared drive on a LAN server.
   
   The machine on which you want to install must be able to share
   the WebSphere MQ Server CD, or a copy of the files on it, and
   you must be able to execute a command on that machine.
   
   If you are running WebSphere MQ on Windows Vista or Windows
   Server 2008 with User Account Control (UAC) enabled, you must
   invoke the silent installation from an elevated command prompt.
   Elevate a command prompt by using a right-click to start the
   command prompt and choose Run as administrator. If you try to
   silently install from a non-elevated command prompt, the install
   fails with an error of AMQ4353 in the install log.
   
   To perform a silent install of IBM WebSphere Eclipse Platform
   supplied with WebSphere MQ without using the launchpad, you need
   to run msiexec with command line parameters. see: Using command
   line parameters with msiexec
   
   An example of a possible msiexec command for the silent
   installation of the WebSphere Eclipse Platform is:
   msiexec.exe /qn /i "D:\Prereqs\IES\MSI\IBM WebSphere Eclipse
   Platform V3.0.msi" ADDLOCAL="Base" AGREETOLICENSE="yes" /l*v
   c:\

question:
Silent uninstall of ITCAM for MQ agent fails

Running silent uninstall of the ITCAM for MQ agent with this command: start /wait setup /z"/sfMQ_Silent_Uninstall.txt" /s /f2"C:\temp\silent_setup.log" fails with this message in the Abort_*.trc file: SEVERE: You must agree to the License Agreement.

The MQ_Silent_Uninstall.txt does contain this line: License Agreement=I agree to use the software only in accordance with the installed license.

Give a concise technical answer. In the final answer, state the concrete fix or rule; omit the reasoning and introductory phrases.

gold.answer: Specify the complete path to the silent response file while launching the silent install.

answer:
**Fix:** Use the full absolute path to the response file in the `/z` parameter.

In the failing command the file is referenced as `/sfMQ_Silent_Uninstall.txt` (a relative/bare filename). The installer cannot locate and parse the file, so it never reads the `License Agreement=I agree…` line and aborts.

Change the command to, for example:

```
start /wait setup /z"C:\temp\sfMQ_Silent_Uninstall.txt" /s /f2"C:\temp\silent_setup.log"
```

**Rule:** The `/z` argument must contain the complete drive-letter path to the silent response file; a relative or pathless filename will not be found, causing the installer to behave as if no response (including the license-acceptance line) was supplied.

question:
Silent uninstall of ITCAM for MQ agent fails

Running silent uninstall of the ITCAM for MQ agent with this command: start /wait setup /z"/sfMQ_Silent_Uninstall.txt" /s /f2"C:\temp\silent_setup.log" fails with this message in the Abort_*.trc file: SEVERE: You must agree to the License Agreement.

The MQ_Silent_Uninstall.txt does contain this line: License Agreement=I agree to use the software only in accordance with the installed license.

Give a concise technical answer. In the final answer, state the concrete fix or rule; omit the reasoning and introductory phrases.

gold.answer: Specify the complete path to the silent response file while launching the silent install.

answer:
**Fix:** Use the full absolute path to the response file in the `/z` parameter.

In the failing command the file is referenced as `/sfMQ_Silent_Uninstall.txt` (a relative/bare filename). The installer cannot locate and parse the file, so it never reads the `License Agreement=I agree…` line and aborts.

Change the command to, for example:

```
start /wait setup /z"C:\temp\sfMQ_Silent_Uninstall.txt" /s /f2"C:\temp\silent_setup.log"
```

**Rule:** The `/z` argument must contain the complete drive-letter path to the silent response file; a relative or pathless filename will not be found, causing the installer to behave as if no response (including the license-acceptance line) was supplied.

sources.text:
Installer (MSI). You can invoke MSI directly, without using the
   WebSphere MQ Installation Launchpad. This means that you can
   install WebSphere Eclipse Platform on a machine without
   interaction. This process is called unattended (or silent)
   installation, and is particularly useful for installing
   WebSphere Eclipse Platform over a network on a remote machine,
   because you can install from a shared drive on a LAN server.
   
   The machine on which you want to install must be able to share
   the WebSphere MQ Server CD, or a copy of the files on it, and
   you must be able to execute a command on that machine.
   
   If you are running WebSphere MQ on Windows Vista or Windows
   Server 2008 with User Account Control (UAC) enabled, you must
   invoke the silent installation from an elevated command prompt.
   Elevate a command prompt by using a right-click to start the
   command prompt and choose Run as administrator. If you try to
   silently install from a non-elevated command prompt, the install
   fails with an error of AMQ4353 in the install log.
   
   To perform a silent install of IBM WebSphere Eclipse Platform
   supplied with WebSphere MQ without using the launchpad, you need
   to run msiexec with command line parameters. see: Using command
   line parameters with msiexec
   
   An example of a possible msiexec command for the silent
   installation of the WebSphere Eclipse Platform is:
   msiexec.exe /qn /i "D:\Prereqs\IES\MSI\IBM WebSphere Eclipse
   Platform V3.0.msi" ADDLOCAL="Base" AGREETOLICENSE="yes" /l*v
   c:\

question:
Silent uninstall of ITCAM for MQ agent fails

Running silent uninstall of the ITCAM for MQ agent with this command: start /wait setup /z"/sfMQ_Silent_Uninstall.txt" /s /f2"C:\temp\silent_setup.log" fails with this message in the Abort_*.trc file: SEVERE: You must agree to the License Agreement.

The MQ_Silent_Uninstall.txt does contain this line: License Agreement=I agree to use the software only in accordance with the installed license.

Give a concise technical answer. In the final answer, state the concrete fix or rule; omit the reasoning and introductory phrases.

gold.answer: Specify the complete path to the silent response file while launching the silent install.

answer: **Save the `sfMQ_Silent_Uninstall.txt` response file in ANSI encoding (not UTF-8/UTF-8 with BOM).** The IBM installation engine's response-file parser does not handle a UTF-8 BOM; it corrupts the first logical token it reads, so the `License Agreement=…` line is effectively not recognized. Open the file in Notepad, use **Save As → Encoding: ANSI**, overwrite the original, and re-run the silent uninstall command.

gold.answer: Specify the complete path to the silent response file while launching the silent install.

answer: **Save the `sfMQ_Silent_Uninstall.txt` response file in ANSI encoding (not UTF-8/UTF-8 with BOM).** The IBM installation engine's response-file parser does not handle a UTF-8 BOM; it corrupts the first logical token it reads, so the `License Agreement=…` line is effectively not recognized. Open the file in Notepad, use **Save As → Encoding: ANSI**, overwrite the original, and re-run the silent uninstall command.

sources.text:
Installer (MSI). You can invoke MSI directly, without using the
   WebSphere MQ Installation Launchpad. This means that you can
   install WebSphere Eclipse Platform on a machine without
   interaction. This process is called unattended (or silent)
   installation, and is particularly useful for installing
   WebSphere Eclipse Platform over a network on a remote machine,
   because you can install from a shared drive on a LAN server.
   
   The machine on which you want to install must be able to share
   the WebSphere MQ Server CD, or a copy of the files on it, and
   you must be able to execute a command on that machine.
   
   If you are running WebSphere MQ on Windows Vista or Windows
   Server 2008 with User Account Control (UAC) enabled, you must
   invoke the silent installation from an elevated command prompt.
   Elevate a command prompt by using a right-click to start the
   command prompt and choose Run as administrator. If you try to
   silently install from a non-elevated command prompt, the install
   fails with an error of AMQ4353 in the install log.
   
   To perform a silent install of IBM WebSphere Eclipse Platform
   supplied with WebSphere MQ without using the launchpad, you need
   to run msiexec with command line parameters. see: Using command
   line parameters with msiexec
   
   An example of a possible msiexec command for the silent
   installation of the WebSphere Eclipse Platform is:
   msiexec.exe /qn /i "D:\Prereqs\IES\MSI\IBM WebSphere Eclipse
   Platform V3.0.msi" ADDLOCAL="Base" AGREETOLICENSE="yes" /l*v
   c:\

gold.answer: Specify the complete path to the silent response file while launching the silent install.

answer:
The `/z` response-file argument must contain the **full path** to the `.txt` file (as shown in the reference: `/z"/sfC:\$user\temp\LO_silent_Install.txt"`). Your command supplies only a bare file name (`/z"/sfMQ_Silent_Uninstall.txt"`), so the installer never locates or reads the file, never sees the `License Agreement=` line, and aborts with "You must agree to the License Agreement."

**Fix:** Provide the absolute path to the response file:

```
start /wait setup /z"/sfC:\temp\MQ_Silent_Uninstall.txt" /s /f2"C:\temp\silent_setup.log"
```

Silent uninstall of ITCAM for MQ agent fails

Running silent uninstall of the ITCAM for MQ agent with this command: start /wait setup /z"/sfMQ_Silent_Uninstall.txt" /s /f2"C:\temp\silent_setup.log" fails with this message in the Abort_*.trc file: SEVERE: You must agree to the License Agreement.

The MQ_Silent_Uninstall.txt does contain this line: License Agreement=I agree to use the software only in accordance with the installed license.

Give a concise technical answer. In the final answer, state the concrete fix or rule; omit the reasoning and introductory phrases.

gold.answer: Specify the complete path to the silent response file while launching the silent install.

answer:
**Fix:** Convert `MQ_Silent_Uninstall.txt` from Unix (LF) line endings to Windows DOS (CRLF) line endings. The installer's response-file parser does not recognize LF-only line terminators, so the `License Agreement=…` line is effectively not read, producing the "You must agree to the License Agreement" abort.

**How to apply:** Re-save the file with CRLF endings (e.g., open in Notepad → Save As → choose "Windows" encoding, or run `unix2dos MQ_Silent_Uninstall.txt`). Do **not** add a trailing blank line; the file must simply end with `0D 0A` after the last entry. Then re-run the silent uninstall command.

Running silent uninstall of the ITCAM for MQ agent with this command: start /wait setup /z"/sfMQ_Silent_Uninstall.txt" /s /f2"C:\temp\silent_setup.log" fails with this message in the Abort_*.trc file: SEVERE: You must agree to the License Agreement.

The MQ_Silent_Uninstall.txt does contain this line: License Agreement=I agree to use the software only in accordance with the installed license.

Give a concise technical answer. In the final answer, state the concrete fix or rule; omit the reasoning and introductory phrases.

gold.answer: Specify the complete path to the silent response file while launching the silent install.

answer:
The response file path in the `/z` parameter is relative (`/sfMQ_Silent_Uninstall.txt`), so the installer cannot locate it and never reads the `License Agreement` property. Specify the **complete (absolute) path** to the silent response file, e.g.:

```
start /wait setup /z"C:\temp\sfMQ_Silent_Uninstall.txt" /s /f2"C:\temp\silent_setup.log"
```

        Protocol1=ip.spipe

        IPPIPE_Port=1918

question:
Silent uninstall of ITCAM for MQ agent fails

Running silent uninstall of the ITCAM for MQ agent with this command: start /wait setup /z"/sfMQ_Silent_Uninstall.txt" /s /f2"C:\temp\silent_setup.log" fails with this message in the Abort_*.trc file: SEVERE: You must agree to the License Agreement.

The MQ_Silent_Uninstall.txt does contain this line: License Agreement=I agree to use the software only in accordance with the installed license.

Give a concise technical answer. In the final answer, state the concrete fix or rule; omit the reasoning and introductory phrases.

gold.answer: Specify the complete path to the silent response file while launching the silent install.

answer:
The silent response file path in the `setup` command must be a **complete (absolute) path**. In the given command, `/z"/sfMQ_Silent_Uninstall.txt"` is not an absolute path, so the installer cannot reliably read the file and never sees the `License Agreement=…` entry, producing the "You must agree to the License Agreement" error.

**Fix:** Specify the full path to the response file, e.g.:

```
start /wait setup /z"C:\temp\MQ_Silent_Uninstall.txt" /s /f2"C:\temp\silent_setup.log"
```

sources.title: IBM IC59041: How to perform a silent install or uninstall of the IBM WebSphere Eclipse platform as supplied with WebSphere MQ. - United States
sources.text:
Installer (MSI). You can invoke MSI directly, without using the
   WebSphere MQ Installation Launchpad. This means that you can
   install WebSphere Eclipse Platform on a machine without
   interaction. This process is called unattended (or silent)
   installation, and is particularly useful for installing
   WebSphere Eclipse Platform over a network on a remote machine,
   because you can install from a shared drive on a LAN server.
   
   The machine on which you want to install must be able to share
   the WebSphere MQ Server CD, or a copy of the files on it, and
   you must be able to execute a command on that machine.
   
   If you are running WebSphere MQ on Windows Vista or Windows
   Server 2008 with User Account Control (UAC) enabled, you must
   invoke the silent installation from an elevated command prompt.
   Elevate a command prompt by using a right-click to start the
   command prompt and choose Run as administrator. If you try to
   silently install from a non-elevated command prompt, the install
   fails with an error of AMQ4353 in the install log.
   
   To perform a silent install of IBM WebSphere Eclipse Platform
   supplied with WebSphere MQ without using the launchpad, you need
   to run msiexec with command line parameters. see: Using command
   line parameters with msiexec
   
   An example of a possible msiexec command for the silent
   installation of the WebSphere Eclipse Platform is:
   msiexec.exe /qn /i "D:\Prereqs\IES\MSI\IBM WebSphere Eclipse
   Platform V3.0.msi" ADDLOCAL="Base" AGREETOLICENSE="yes" /l*v
   c:\

question:
Silent uninstall of ITCAM for MQ agent fails

Running silent uninstall of the ITCAM for MQ agent with this command: start /wait setup /z"/sfMQ_Silent_Uninstall.txt" /s /f2"C:\temp\silent_setup.log" fails with this message in the Abort_*.trc file: SEVERE: You must agree to the License Agreement.

The MQ_Silent_Uninstall.txt does contain this line: License Agreement=I agree to use the software only in accordance with the installed license.

Give a concise technical answer. In the final answer, state the concrete fix or rule; omit the reasoning and introductory phrases.

gold.answer: Specify the complete path to the silent response file while launching the silent install.

answer:
The response file path in the `/z` argument must be a **complete (absolute) path**. In the failing command, `/z"/sfMQ_Silent_Uninstall.txt"` is not a fully qualified path, so the installer cannot reliably read the file and never sees the `License Agreement=...` line.

**Fix:** Use the full path to the response file, e.g.:

```
start /wait setup /z"C:\temp\sfMQ_Silent_Uninstall.txt" /s /f2"C:\temp\silent_setup.log"
```

Always pass the complete path to the silent response file when launching the silent install/uninstall.

question:
Silent uninstall of ITCAM for MQ agent fails

Running silent uninstall of the ITCAM for MQ agent with this command: start /wait setup /z"/sfMQ_Silent_Uninstall.txt" /s /f2"C:\temp\silent_setup.log" fails with this message in the Abort_*.trc file: SEVERE: You must agree to the License Agreement.

The MQ_Silent_Uninstall.txt does contain this line: License Agreement=I agree to use the software only in accordance with the installed license.

Give a concise technical answer. In the final answer, state the concrete fix or rule; omit the reasoning and introductory phrases.

gold.answer: Specify the complete path to the silent response file while launching the silent install.

answer:
The response file path in the `/z` argument must be a **complete (absolute) path**. In the failing command, `/z"/sfMQ_Silent_Uninstall.txt"` is not a fully qualified path, so the installer cannot reliably read the file and never sees the `License Agreement=...` line.

**Fix:** Use the full path to the response file, e.g.:

```
start /wait setup /z"C:\temp\sfMQ_Silent_Uninstall.txt" /s /f2"C:\temp\silent_setup.log"
```

Always pass the complete path to the silent response file when launching the silent install/uninstall.

sources.text:
Installer (MSI). You can invoke MSI directly, without using the
   WebSphere MQ Installation Launchpad. This means that you can
   install WebSphere Eclipse Platform on a machine without
   interaction. This process is called unattended (or silent)
   installation, and is particularly useful for installing
   WebSphere Eclipse Platform over a network on a remote machine,
   because you can install from a shared drive on a LAN server.
   
   The machine on which you want to install must be able to share
   the WebSphere MQ Server CD, or a copy of the files on it, and
   you must be able to execute a command on that machine.
   
   If you are running WebSphere MQ on Windows Vista or Windows
   Server 2008 with User Account Control (UAC) enabled, you must
   invoke the silent installation from an elevated command prompt.
   Elevate a command prompt by using a right-click to start the
   command prompt and choose Run as administrator. If you try to
   silently install from a non-elevated command prompt, the install
   fails with an error of AMQ4353 in the install log.
   
   To perform a silent install of IBM WebSphere Eclipse Platform
   supplied with WebSphere MQ without using the launchpad, you need
   to run msiexec with command line parameters. see: Using command
   line parameters with msiexec
   
   An example of a possible msiexec command for the silent
   installation of the WebSphere Eclipse Platform is:
   msiexec.exe /qn /i "D:\Prereqs\IES\MSI\IBM WebSphere Eclipse
   Platform V3.0.msi" ADDLOCAL="Base" AGREETOLICENSE="yes" /l*v
   c:\

question:
Silent uninstall of ITCAM for MQ agent fails

Running silent uninstall of the ITCAM for MQ agent with this command: start /wait setup /z"/sfMQ_Silent_Uninstall.txt" /s /f2"C:\temp\silent_setup.log" fails with this message in the Abort_*.trc file: SEVERE: You must agree to the License Agreement.

The MQ_Silent_Uninstall.txt does contain this line: License Agreement=I agree to use the software only in accordance with the installed license.

Give a concise technical answer. In the final answer, state the concrete fix or rule; omit the reasoning and introductory phrases.

gold.answer: Specify the complete path to the silent response file while launching the silent install.

answer:
**The response-file path in the `/z` argument is invalid.** The command references `/sfMQ_Silent_Uninstall.txt` — a relative path with no drive letter. The installer cannot locate the file, so it never reads the `License Agreement=` line and defaults to the (silent) license check, which fails.

**Fix:** Supply an absolute Windows path to the response file:

```
start /wait setup /z"C:\temp\sfMQ_Silent_Uninstall.txt" /s /f2"C:\temp\silent_setup.log"
```

(adjust the drive/folder to wherever the `.txt` actually resides). Verify the file is plain ANSI text with CRLF line-endings and that the line reads exactly:

```
License Agreement=I agree to use the software only in accordance with the installed license.
```

gold.answer: Specify the complete path to the silent response file while launching the silent install.

answer:
**The response-file path in the `/z` argument is invalid.** The command references `/sfMQ_Silent_Uninstall.txt` — a relative path with no drive letter. The installer cannot locate the file, so it never reads the `License Agreement=` line and defaults to the (silent) license check, which fails.

**Fix:** Supply an absolute Windows path to the response file:

```
start /wait setup /z"C:\temp\sfMQ_Silent_Uninstall.txt" /s /f2"C:\temp\silent_setup.log"
```

(adjust the drive/folder to wherever the `.txt` actually resides). Verify the file is plain ANSI text with CRLF line-endings and that the line reads exactly:

```
License Agreement=I agree to use the software only in accordance with the installed license.
```

sources.text:
Installer (MSI). You can invoke MSI directly, without using the
   WebSphere MQ Installation Launchpad. This means that you can
   install WebSphere Eclipse Platform on a machine without
   interaction. This process is called unattended (or silent)
   installation, and is particularly useful for installing
   WebSphere Eclipse Platform over a network on a remote machine,
   because you can install from a shared drive on a LAN server.
   
   The machine on which you want to install must be able to share
   the WebSphere MQ Server CD, or a copy of the files on it, and
   you must be able to execute a command on that machine.
   
   If you are running WebSphere MQ on Windows Vista or Windows
   Server 2008 with User Account Control (UAC) enabled, you must
   invoke the silent installation from an elevated command prompt.
   Elevate a command prompt by using a right-click to start the
   command prompt and choose Run as administrator. If you try to
   silently install from a non-elevated command prompt, the install
   fails with an error of AMQ4353 in the install log.
   
   To perform a silent install of IBM WebSphere Eclipse Platform
   supplied with WebSphere MQ without using the launchpad, you need
   to run msiexec with command line parameters. see: Using command
   line parameters with msiexec
   
   An example of a possible msiexec command for the silent
   installation of the WebSphere Eclipse Platform is:
   msiexec.exe /qn /i "D:\Prereqs\IES\MSI\IBM WebSphere Eclipse
   Platform V3.0.msi" ADDLOCAL="Base" AGREETOLICENSE="yes" /l*v
   c:\

Running silent uninstall of the ITCAM for MQ agent with this command: start /wait setup /z"/sfMQ_Silent_Uninstall.txt" /s /f2"C:\temp\silent_setup.log" fails with this message in the Abort_*.trc file: SEVERE: You must agree to the License Agreement.

gold.answer: Specify the complete path to the silent response file while launching the silent install.

answer:
**Fix:** Use a full absolute path to the response file in the `/z` parameter. The failing command uses a relative filename (`/sfMQ_Silent_Uninstall.txt`), so `setup.exe` cannot locate the file and never reads the `License Agreement=` line, producing the "You must agree to the License Agreement" error.

Corrected command:

```
start /wait setup /z"/sfC:\temp\MQ_Silent_Uninstall.txt" /s /f2"C:\temp\silent_setup.log"
```

This mirrors the working pattern shown in IBM's reference (e.g., `/z"/sfC:\$user\temp\LO_silent_Install.txt"`), where the response file is specified with a complete path.

The MQ_Silent_Uninstall.txt does contain this line: License Agreement=I agree to use the software only in accordance with the installed license.

Give a concise technical answer. In the final answer, state the concrete fix or rule; omit the reasoning and introductory phrases.

gold.answer: Specify the complete path to the silent response file while launching the silent install.

answer:
**Save the `MQ_Silent_Uninstall.txt` file in ANSI (Windows-1252) encoding, not UTF-8 or UTF-8 with BOM.**

ITCAM's installer is built on InstallShield, which reads the silent response file using the system ANSI code page. A UTF-8 BOM (or any non-ANSI encoding) corrupts the first line/entire file parsing, so the `License Agreement=…` entry is never matched, and the installer aborts with "You must agree to the License Agreement."

Fix:

1. Open `MQ_Silent_Uninstall.txt` in Notepad (or Notepad++).
2. **File → Save As → Encoding: ANSI** (do **not** choose "UTF-8 with BOM" or plain "UTF-8").
3. Confirm the line reads exactly (no trailing spaces, Windows line endings CRLF):
   ```
   License Agreement=I agree to use the software only in accordance with the installed license.
   ```
4. Re-run the silent uninstall command.

gold.answer: Specify the complete path to the silent response file while launching the silent install.

answer:
**Fix:** Use the **full (absolute) path** to the silent response file in the `setup` command. The command as given uses a relative path (`/z"/sfMQ_Silent_Uninstall.txt"`), so the installer cannot locate/read the file, never sees the `License Agreement=I agree…` line, and aborts with the license error.

Change the command to:

```
start /wait setup /z"C:\path\to\sfMQ_Silent_Uninstall.txt" /s /f2"C:\temp\silent_setup.log"
```

where `C:\path\to\` is the actual directory containing `sfMQ_Silent_Uninstall.txt`.

question:
How to configure DC to look on a different App server for the SSP?



I have a single Application server with the RES console installed, and then a separate application server with the XU, the ssp ear, etc. on that one. Each app server is configured separately with respective ports. for example, mgmt server (with the RES console only) has port 8000, and the runtime server (with all of the runtime components) has port 9000.

The problem I am running into is the following:

When I am trying to run a DVS test suite from Decision Center against RES, (my server endpoint in Decision Center is configured as http://hostname:port/res)

I am getting a "the host and port are responsive but the "/testing/sspService" cannot be found. This is expected if it is looking on the same server as the RES console since the application (ssp) is not deployed there.

However, I cannot seem to configure the RES console to not assume that the ssp is running on the same port.

gold.answer:
First remember to pack all your XOMs (eXecutable Object Model) into the ssp.war following the documentation [http://publib.boulder.ibm.com/infocenter/brjrules/v7r1/topic/com.ibm.websphere.ilog.jrules.doc/Content/Business_Rules/Documentation/_pubskel/JRules/ps_JRules_Global720.html]. 

Then make sure the SSP (ssp.war) is deployed on each server along with a XU connection factory and the appropriate datasource definition. 

 

Then create your own SSP resolver, add it to the teamserver.war and set the teamserver.defaultSSPResolver.class property to this class following this specification [http://publib.boulder.ibm.com/infocenter/brjrules/v7r1/index.jsp?topic=/com.ibm.websphere.ilog.jrules.doc/html/api/html/ilog/rules/teamserver/model/testing/IlrSSPResolver.html]. 

 

By implementing your own method IlrSSPResolver.getSSPURL(String serverName,URL url), you will be able to point to something else than the default provider. 

The default provider uses the url of the Rule Execution Server passed in parameter and replaces the application name with testing. 

A simple implementation can use the server name to return a specific server URL.

# Configuring Decision Center to Point to a Different App Server for the SSP

## The Root Cause

When you configure your Decision Center server endpoint as `http://hostname:8000/res`, the DVS test runner uses that **same host and port** to resolve the SSP service at `/testing/sspService`. Since the SSP EAR is deployed on your **runtime** server (port 9000), not on the **mgmt/RES-console** server (port 8000), the lookup fails.

## The Solution: Customize `IlrSSPResolver`

Per the IBM support documentation (SWG21615508), the mechanism to redirect DVS test execution to a different application server is to **customize the `IlrSSPResolver` class**:

> *"Customize IlrSSPResolver if you want to distribute the DVS tests to multiple application servers."*

### Step-by-step

1. **Locate the resolver class.**
   `IlrSSPResolver` (or a subclass you create) lives in the ODM/DR runtime library. Find it in the codebase shipped with your ODM install (typically under the runtime/libraries or `com.ibm.rules.resolver` / `com.ibm.rules.ssp` packages).

2. **Override the endpoint-resolution method.**
   The class contains a method (commonly `resolve()`, `getEndpoint()`, or similar) that builds the URL by taking the host and port from the configured server endpoint and appending `testing/sspService`. Override that method so it returns the **runtime** server's address instead:

   ```
   http://<runtime-hostname>:9000/ssp/testing/sspService
   ```

   Rather than the (incorrect) default:

   ```
   http://<mgmt-hostname>:8000/res/testing/sspService
   ```

3. **Deploy the customized resolver.**
   Build the modified class into the appropriate EAR/JAR on the **mgmt** server (the one running the RES console / Decision Center), and restart that server. The resolver is consulted *from* the DC side when it dispatches a DVS test run, so it only needs to be on the server that hosts the DC/RES console.

4. **Verify.**
   Re-run a DVS test suite from Decision Center. The DC console should now hit `http://<runtime-host

Title: IBM "The host appears to be running but port "-1" does not respond. " error when testing connection to Rule Execution Server from Decision Center - United States

Text:
 TECHNOTE (TROUBLESHOOTING)

PROBLEM(ABSTRACT)
 In the Decision Center Configure tab, under Manage Servers, when I test the connection to the server instance of the Rule Execution Server, I see the error:
Test failed for server foo. The host appears to be running but port "-1" does not respond. 

RESOLVING THE PROBLEM
Make sure that the server connection details are correctly specified ( hostname, portnumber, username/password) in the Decision Center Configure tab, under Manage Servers.


 * Ensure that you set the URL of the Rule Execution Server to be http://‹host›:‹port›/res, not http://‹host›:‹port›/testing 
 * Check that the port is not being used by another process [http://www.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21443946]. If it is, stop the other process. 
 * Make sure that the user belongs to a Decision Center group that has privileges [http://pic.dhe.ibm.com/infocenter/dmanager/v8r5m1/index.jsp?topic=%2Fcom.ibm.odm.dcenter.bu.econsole%2Ftopics%2Ftsk_config_deploy_servers.html] to access a RES server 
 * Make sure that the SSP application (jrules-ssp-‹appserver›.ear) has been installed correctly on the application server, and has been started. 
 * Test the availability of Decision Validation Services by typing the URL in your browser: http://‹host›:‹port›/testing 
 * Make sure there is no firewall blocking the HTTP/HTTPS connection from Decision

Title: IBM Unable to run Test Suites against clustered SSP from Decison Center console - United States

Text:
 TECHNOTE (TROUBLESHOOTING)

PROBLEM(ABSTRACT)
 I have a clustered Decision Server where XU and SSP are deployed on cluster members and Rule Execution Server (RES) console is deployed on a standalone server outside of the cluster. IHS and a load balancer is configured on top of the cluster. 
In Decision Center, the RES server URL is configured with the load balanced IP.
Test Suite fails to run from Decision Center console in this configuration. 

SYMPTOM
After clicking on Run from Decision Center console, the process starts, but after a few seconds, execution stops with a message: Cannot execute the scenario suite xxx. The operation was aborted by user. 

No errors shown in Decision Center and Decision Server server logs. The only error seen is from the browser and no stack trace is displayed.


CAUSE
There are multiple http requests made from Decision Center to SSP in order to start the test suite run and check its status. When a load balancer is used, it is not guaranteed that each http request from the Decision Center is routed to the same SSP. For instance, assume the first http request is received by SSP1. Decision Center later makes another http request to check on its status by contacting the same URL. This request can be load balanced to SSP2, which has no notion of the job. Such scenario can lead to the aforementioned error. 


RESOLVING THE PROBLEM
Run test suite from Decision Center with either one of the following configurations: 

1. Run the Decision Validation Service (DVS) test against a dedicated standalone SSP: 
Deploy SSP on the same server with RES management console. On Decision Center console, configure RES server URL to point to the specific server IP, instead of the load balanced IP.

Title: IBM Error when executing DVS test from RTS:  "Host and port appear to be responsive but the service "/testing/repositoryService" does not exist." - United States

Text:
 TECHNOTE (TROUBLESHOOTING)

PROBLEM(ABSTRACT)
 When I run a DVS test from RTS, I get the following error: "Host and port appear to be responsive but the service "/testing/repositoryService" does not exist."


RESOLVING THE PROBLEM
 

This might be due to user errors in configuration. For example, you could have set the URL of the Rule Execution Server to be 'http://‹host›:‹port›/testing' instead of 'http://‹host›:‹port›/res" in the RTS configuration. 

. When you add a new server to the RTS configuration ( Websphere ILOG Rule Team Server online help › Configure: Manage your project configuration › Managing servers [http://publib.boulder.ibm.com/infocenter/brdotnet/v7r0m2/index.jsp?topic=/com.ibm.websphere.ilog.brdotnet.doc/Content/Business_Rules/Documentation/_pubskel/Rules_for_DotNET/ps_RFDN_Global716.html]), make sure you specify the URL of the Rule Execution Server (e.g.: http://localhost:8080/res). 

A common mistake is to specify the URL of the SSP server (e.g.: http://localhost:8080/testing), which leads to the error above. 

 

This error could also indicate that the SSP is not correctly deployed or configured. 

Please check that the SSP is correctly deployed and configured. 

Examine the application server logs for error messages which indicate the root of the problem. For example, you could have multiple SSPs deployed and different XOMs

the process starts, but after a few seconds, execution stops with a message: Cannot execute the scenario suite xxx. The operation was aborted by user. 

No errors shown in Decision Center and Decision Server server logs. The only error seen is from the browser and no stack trace is displayed.


CAUSE
There are multiple http requests made from Decision Center to SSP in order to start the test suite run and check its status. When a load balancer is used, it is not guaranteed that each http request from the Decision Center is routed to the same SSP. For instance, assume the first http request is received by SSP1. Decision Center later makes another http request to check on its status by contacting the same URL. This request can be load balanced to SSP2, which has no notion of the job. Such scenario can lead to the aforementioned error. 


RESOLVING THE PROBLEM
Run test suite from Decision Center with either one of the following configurations: 

1. Run the Decision Validation Service (DVS) test against a dedicated standalone SSP: 
Deploy SSP on the same server with RES management console. On Decision Center console, configure RES server URL to point to the specific server IP, instead of the load balanced IP. 

2. Customize IlrSSPResolver if you want to distribute the DVS tests to multiple application servers. Note that all rule executions for each single Test Suite or Simulation request will still be done on the same server. This customization allows load balancing between Test Suite or Simulation requests.
See this document [http://www-01.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21502095] for details.
