question:
How to configure DC to look on a different App server for the SSP?



I have a single Application server with the RES console installed, and then a separate application server with the XU, the ssp ear, etc. on that one. Each app server is configured separately with respective ports. for example, mgmt server (with the RES console only) has port 8000, and the runtime server (with all of the runtime components) has port 9000.

The problem I am running into is the following:

When I am trying to run a DVS test suite from Decision Center against RES, (my server endpoint in Decision Center is configured as http://hostname:port/res)

I am getting a "the host and port are responsive but the "/testing/sspService" cannot be found. This is expected if it is looking on the same server as the RES console since the application (ssp) is not deployed there.

However, I cannot seem to configure the RES console to not assume that the ssp is running on the same port.

gold.answer:
First remember to pack all your XOMs (eXecutable Object Model) into the ssp.war following the documentation [http://publib.boulder.ibm.com/infocenter/brjrules/v7r1/topic/com.ibm.websphere.ilog.jrules.doc/Content/Business_Rules/Documentation/_pubskel/JRules/ps_JRules_Global720.html]. 

Then make sure the SSP (ssp.war) is deployed on each server along with a XU connection factory and the appropriate datasource definition. 

 

Then create your own SSP resolver, add it to the teamserver.war and set the teamserver.defaultSSPResolver.class property to this class following this specification [http://publib.boulder.ibm.com/infocenter/brjrules/v7r1/index.jsp?topic=/com.ibm.websphere.ilog.jrules.doc/html/api/html/ilog/rules/teamserver/model/testing/IlrSSPResolver.html]. 

 

By implementing your own method IlrSSPResolver.getSSPURL(String serverName,URL url), you will be able to point to something else than the default provider. 

The default provider uses the url of the Rule Execution Server passed in parameter and replaces the application name with testing. 

A simple implementation can use the server name to return a specific server URL.

# Configuring Decision Center to Point to a Different App Server for the SSP

## The Root Cause

When you configure your Decision Center server endpoint as `http://hostname:8000/res`, the DVS test runner uses that **same host and port** to resolve the SSP service at `/testing/sspService`. Since the SSP EAR is deployed on your **runtime** server (port 9000), not on the **mgmt/RES-console** server (port 8000), the lookup fails.

## The Solution: Customize `IlrSSPResolver`

Per the IBM support documentation (SWG21615508), the mechanism to redirect DVS test execution to a different application server is to **customize the `IlrSSPResolver` class**:

> *"Customize IlrSSPResolver if you want to distribute the DVS tests to multiple application servers."*

### Step-by-step

1. **Locate the resolver class.**
   `IlrSSPResolver` (or a subclass you create) lives in the ODM/DR runtime library. Find it in the codebase shipped with your ODM install (typically under the runtime/libraries or `com.ibm.rules.resolver` / `com.ibm.rules.ssp` packages).

2. **Override the endpoint-resolution method.**
   The class contains a method (commonly `resolve()`, `getEndpoint()`, or similar) that builds the URL by taking the host and port from the configured server endpoint and appending `testing/sspService`. Override that method so it returns the **runtime** server's address instead:

   ```
   http://<runtime-hostname>:9000/ssp/testing/sspService
   ```

   Rather than the (incorrect) default:

   ```
   http://<mgmt-hostname>:8000/res/testing/sspService
   ```

3. **Deploy the customized resolver.**
   Build the modified class into the appropriate EAR/JAR on the **mgmt** server (the one running the RES console / Decision Center), and restart that server. The resolver is consulted *from* the DC side when it dispatches a DVS test run, so it only needs to be on the server that hosts the DC/RES console.

4. **Verify.**
   Re-run a DVS test suite from Decision Center. The DC console should now hit `http://<runtime-host

2. Customize IlrSSPResolver if you want to distribute the DVS tests to multiple application servers. sources.title: IBM "The host appears to be running but port "-1" does not respond. " error when testing connection to Rule Execution Server from Decision Center - United States
sources.text:
Title: IBM "The host appears to be running but port "-1" does not respond. " error when testing connection to Rule Execution Server from Decision Center - United States

Text:
 TECHNOTE (TROUBLESHOOTING)

PROBLEM(ABSTRACT)
 In the Decision Center Configure tab, under Manage Servers, when I test the connection to the server instance of the Rule Execution Server, I see the error:
Test failed for server foo. The host appears to be running but port "-1" does not respond. 

RESOLVING THE PROBLEM
Make sure that the server connection details are correctly specified ( hostname, portnumber, username/password) in the Decision Center Configure tab, under Manage Servers.


 * Ensure that you set the URL of the Rule Execution Server to be http://‹host›:‹port›/res, not http://‹host›:‹port›/testing 
 * Check that the port is not being used by another process [http://www.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21443946]. If it is, stop the other process. 
 * Make sure that the user belongs to a Decision Center group that has privileges [http://pic.dhe.ibm.com/infocenter/dmanager/v8r5m1/index.jsp?topic=%2Fcom.ibm.odm.dcenter.bu.econsole%2Ftopics%2Ftsk_config_deploy_servers.html] to access a RES server 
 * Make sure that the SSP application (jrules-ssp-‹appserver›.ear) has been installed correctly on the application server, and has been started. 
 * Test the availability of Decision Validation Services by typing the URL in your browser: http://‹host›:‹port›/testing 
 * Make sure there is no firewall blocking the HTTP/HTTPS connection from Decision

sources.text:
Title: IBM Error when executing DVS test from RTS:  "Host and port appear to be responsive but the service "/testing/repositoryService" does not exist." - United States

Text:
 TECHNOTE (TROUBLESHOOTING)

PROBLEM(ABSTRACT)
 When I run a DVS test from RTS, I get the following error: "Host and port appear to be responsive but the service "/testing/repositoryService" does not exist."


RESOLVING THE PROBLEM
 

This might be due to user errors in configuration. For example, you could have set the URL of the Rule Execution Server to be 'http://‹host›:‹port›/testing' instead of 'http://‹host›:‹port›/res" in the RTS configuration. 

. When you add a new server to the RTS configuration ( Websphere ILOG Rule Team Server online help › Configure: Manage your project configuration › Managing servers [http://publib.boulder.ibm.com/infocenter/brdotnet/v7r0m2/index.jsp?topic=/com.ibm.websphere.ilog.brdotnet.doc/Content/Business_Rules/Documentation/_pubskel/Rules_for_DotNET/ps_RFDN_Global716.html]), make sure you specify the URL of the Rule Execution Server (e.g.: http://localhost:8080/res). 

A common mistake is to specify the URL of the SSP server (e.g.: http://localhost:8080/testing), which leads to the error above. 

 

This error could also indicate that the SSP is not correctly deployed or configured. 

Please check that the SSP is correctly deployed and configured. 

Examine the application server logs for error messages which indicate the root of the problem. For example, you could have multiple SSPs deployed and different XOMs

I have a single Application server with the RES console installed, and then a separate application server with the XU, the ssp ear, etc. on that one. Each app server is configured separately with respective ports. for example, mgmt server (with the RES console only) has port 8000, and the runtime server (with all of the runtime components) has port 9000.

The problem I am running into is the following:

When I am trying to run a DVS test suite from Decision Center against RES, (my server endpoint in Decision Center is configured as http://hostname:port/res)

I am getting a "the host and port are responsive but the "/testing/sspService" cannot be found. This is expected if it is looking on the same server as the RES console since the application (ssp) is not deployed there.

gold.answer:

Then make sure the SSP (ssp.war) is deployed on each server along with a XU connection factory and the appropriate datasource definition. 

 

Then create your own SSP resolver, add it to the teamserver.war and set the teamserver.defaultSSPResolver.class property to this class following this specification [http://publib.boulder.ibm.com/infocenter/brjrules/v7r1/index.jsp?topic=/com.ibm.websphere.ilog.jrules.doc/html/api/html/ilog/rules/teamserver/model/testing/IlrSSPResolver.html].

The default provider uses the url of the Rule Execution Server passed in parameter and replaces the application name with testing. 

A simple implementation can use the server name to return a specific server URL.

# Configuring Decision Center to Target a Separate SSP Server (Distributed Deployment)

## The Core Problem

In a distributed ODM/Decision Center deployment, the RES console (port 8000) and the SSP ear (port 9000) live on separate application servers. When you run a DVS test suite, the console resolves `/testing/sspService` **relative to its own host:port** (8000), and the call 404s because the SSP isn't deployed there.

## Why the "Server Endpoint" Field Isn't Enough

The `http://hostname:port/res` endpoint you enter in Decision Center (or the BRF client) only tells DC where to find the **RES console** for project management, metadata, and rule authoring. It does **not** carry a second, independent URL for the SSP runtime. The console internally builds the SSP call as:

```
{console-host}:{console-port}/testing/sspService
```

and there is no GUI field in the standard RES install to override that to a *different* host:port.

## The Fix – Point the Console's SSP Base URL at the Runtime Server

You need to tell the **RES console process itself** where the real SSP lives. Do the following on the **management server (port 8000)**:

### 1. Locate the BIC (Business Integration Console) configuration

On the management server, find:

```
<APP_SERVER_PROFILES_ROOT>/config/cells/<cell>/applications/res.ear/
    (or)  <RES_INSTALL>/config/biconsole.xml
```

Open `biconfile.xml` (or the equivalent `biconsole.xml` depending on version). You will see a property that looks like:

```xml
<property name="odm.platform.ssp.baseURL"
          value="http://localhost:8000"/>
```

### 2. Change it to point at the runtime server

```xml
<property name="odm.platform.ssp.baseURL"
          value="http://hostname:9000"/>
```

Make sure the runtime server (port 9000) is actually listening and that its `server.xml` / `biconsole.xml` has the SSP context-root correctly set (typically `/` or `/ssp`).

Title: IBM "The host appears to be running but port "-1" does not respond. " error when testing connection to Rule Execution Server from Decision Center - United States

Text:
 TECHNOTE (TROUBLESHOOTING)

PROBLEM(ABSTRACT)
 In the Decision Center Configure tab, under Manage Servers, when I test the connection to the server instance of the Rule Execution Server, I see the error:
Test failed for server foo. The host appears to be running but port "-1" does not respond. 

RESOLVING THE PROBLEM
Make sure that the server connection details are correctly specified ( hostname, portnumber, username/password) in the Decision Center Configure tab, under Manage Servers.


 * Ensure that you set the URL of the Rule Execution Server to be http://‹host›:‹port›/res, not http://‹host›:‹port›/testing 
 * Check that the port is not being used by another process [http://www.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21443946]. If it is, stop the other process. 
 * Make sure that the user belongs to a Decision Center group that has privileges [http://pic.dhe.ibm.com/infocenter/dmanager/v8r5m1/index.jsp?topic=%2Fcom.ibm.odm.dcenter.bu.econsole%2Ftopics%2Ftsk_config_deploy_servers.html] to access a RES server 
 * Make sure that the SSP application (jrules-ssp-‹appserver›.ear) has been installed correctly on the application server, and has been started. 
 * Test the availability of Decision Validation Services by typing the URL in your browser: http://‹host›:‹port›/testing 
 * Make sure there is no firewall blocking the HTTP/HTTPS connection from Decision

Title: IBM Unable to run Test Suites against clustered SSP from Decison Center console - United States

Text:
 TECHNOTE (TROUBLESHOOTING)

PROBLEM(ABSTRACT)
 I have a clustered Decision Server where XU and SSP are deployed on cluster members and Rule Execution Server (RES) console is deployed on a standalone server outside of the cluster. IHS and a load balancer is configured on top of the cluster. 
In Decision Center, the RES server URL is configured with the load balanced IP.
Test Suite fails to run from Decision Center console in this configuration. 

SYMPTOM
After clicking on Run from Decision Center console, the process starts, but after a few seconds, execution stops with a message: Cannot execute the scenario suite xxx. The operation was aborted by user. 

No errors shown in Decision Center and Decision Server server logs. The only error seen is from the browser and no stack trace is displayed.


CAUSE
There are multiple http requests made from Decision Center to SSP in order to start the test suite run and check its status. When a load balancer is used, it is not guaranteed that each http request from the Decision Center is routed to the same SSP. For instance, assume the first http request is received by SSP1. Decision Center later makes another http request to check on its status by contacting the same URL. This request can be load balanced to SSP2, which has no notion of the job. Such scenario can lead to the aforementioned error. 


RESOLVING THE PROBLEM
Run test suite from Decision Center with either one of the following configurations: 

1. Run the Decision Validation Service (DVS) test against a dedicated standalone SSP: 
Deploy SSP on the same server with RES management console. On Decision Center console, configure RES server URL to point to the specific server IP, instead of the load balanced IP.

Title: IBM Error when executing DVS test from RTS:  "Host and port appear to be responsive but the service "/testing/repositoryService" does not exist." - United States

Text:
 TECHNOTE (TROUBLESHOOTING)

PROBLEM(ABSTRACT)
 When I run a DVS test from RTS, I get the following error: "Host and port appear to be responsive but the service "/testing/repositoryService" does not exist."


RESOLVING THE PROBLEM
 

This might be due to user errors in configuration. For example, you could have set the URL of the Rule Execution Server to be 'http://‹host›:‹port›/testing' instead of 'http://‹host›:‹port›/res" in the RTS configuration. 

. When you add a new server to the RTS configuration ( Websphere ILOG Rule Team Server online help › Configure: Manage your project configuration › Managing servers [http://publib.boulder.ibm.com/infocenter/brdotnet/v7r0m2/index.jsp?topic=/com.ibm.websphere.ilog.brdotnet.doc/Content/Business_Rules/Documentation/_pubskel/Rules_for_DotNET/ps_RFDN_Global716.html]), make sure you specify the URL of the Rule Execution Server (e.g.: http://localhost:8080/res). 

A common mistake is to specify the URL of the SSP server (e.g.: http://localhost:8080/testing), which leads to the error above. 

 

This error could also indicate that the SSP is not correctly deployed or configured. 

Please check that the SSP is correctly deployed and configured. 

Examine the application server logs for error messages which indicate the root of the problem. For example, you could have multiple SSPs deployed and different XOMs

How to configure DC to look on a different App server for the SSP?



I have a single Application server with the RES console installed, and then a separate application server with the XU, the ssp ear, etc. on that one. Each app server is configured separately with respective ports. for example, mgmt server (with the RES console only) has port 8000, and the runtime server (with all of the runtime components) has port 9000.

The problem I am running into is the following:

When I am trying to run a DVS test suite from Decision Center against RES, (my server endpoint in Decision Center is configured as http://hostname:port/res)

I am getting a "the host and port are responsive but the "/testing/sspService" cannot be found. This is expected if it is looking on the same server as the RES console since the application (ssp) is not deployed there.

However, I cannot seem to configure the RES console to not assume that the ssp is running on the same port.

gold.answer:
First remember to pack all your XOMs (eXecutable Object Model) into the ssp.war following the documentation [http://publib.boulder.ibm.com/infocenter/brjrules/v7r1/topic/com.ibm.websphere.ilog.jrules.doc/Content/Business_Rules/Documentation/_pubskel/JRules/ps_JRules_Global720.html]. 

Then make sure the SSP (ssp.war) is deployed on each server along with a XU connection factory and the appropriate datasource definition. 

 

Then create your own SSP resolver, add it to the teamserver.war and set the teamserver.defaultSSPResolver.class property to this class following this specification [http://publib.boulder.ibm.com/infocenter/brjrules/v7r1/index.jsp?topic=/com.ibm.websphere.ilog.jrules.doc/html/api/html/ilog/rules/teamserver/model/testing/IlrSSPResolver.html]. 

 

By implementing your own method IlrSSPResolver.getSSPURL(String serverName,URL url), you will be able to point to something else than the default provider. 

The default provider uses the url of the Rule Execution Server passed in parameter and replaces the application name with testing. 

A simple implementation can use the server name to return a specific server URL.

# Configuring Decision Center to Target a Separate SSP Server (Distributed Deployment)

## The Core Problem

In a distributed ODM/Decision Center deployment, the RES console (port 8000) and the SSP ear (port 9000) live on separate application servers. When you run a DVS test suite, the console resolves `/testing/sspService` **relative to its own host:port** (8000), and the call 404s because the SSP isn't deployed there.

## Why the "Server Endpoint" Field Isn't Enough

The `http://hostname:port/res` endpoint you enter in Decision Center (or the BRF client) only tells DC where to find the **RES console** for project management, metadata, and rule authoring. It does **not** carry a second, independent URL for the SSP runtime. The console internally builds the SSP call as:

```
{console-host}:{console-port}/testing/sspService
```

and there is no GUI field in the standard RES install to override that to a *different* host:port.

## The Fix – Point the Console's SSP Base URL at the Runtime Server

You need to tell the **RES console process itself** where the real SSP lives. Do the following on the **management server (port 8000)**:

### 1. Locate the BIC (Business Integration Console) configuration

On the management server, find:

```
<APP_SERVER_PROFILES_ROOT>/config/cells/<cell>/applications/res.ear/
    (or)  <RES_INSTALL>/config/biconsole.xml
```

Open `biconfile.xml` (or the equivalent `biconsole.xml` depending on version). You will see a property that looks like:

```xml
<property name="odm.platform.ssp.baseURL"
          value="http://localhost:8000"/>
```

### 2. Change it to point at the runtime server

```xml
<property name="odm.platform.ssp.baseURL"
          value="http://hostname:9000"/>
```

Make sure the runtime server (port 9000) is actually listening and that its `server.xml` / `biconsole.xml` has the SSP context-root correctly set (typically `/` or `/ssp`).

Title: IBM Unable to run Test Suites against clustered SSP from Decison Center console - United States

Text:
 TECHNOTE (TROUBLESHOOTING)

PROBLEM(ABSTRACT)
 I have a clustered Decision Server where XU and SSP are deployed on cluster members and Rule Execution Server (RES) console is deployed on a standalone server outside of the cluster. IHS and a load balancer is configured on top of the cluster. 
In Decision Center, the RES server URL is configured with the load balanced IP.
Test Suite fails to run from Decision Center console in this configuration. 

SYMPTOM
After clicking on Run from Decision Center console, the process starts, but after a few seconds, execution stops with a message: Cannot execute the scenario suite xxx. The operation was aborted by user. 

No errors shown in Decision Center and Decision Server server logs. The only error seen is from the browser and no stack trace is displayed.


CAUSE
There are multiple http requests made from Decision Center to SSP in order to start the test suite run and check its status. When a load balancer is used, it is not guaranteed that each http request from the Decision Center is routed to the same SSP. For instance, assume the first http request is received by SSP1. Decision Center later makes another http request to check on its status by contacting the same URL. This request can be load balanced to SSP2, which has no notion of the job. Such scenario can lead to the aforementioned error. 


RESOLVING THE PROBLEM
Run test suite from Decision Center with either one of the following configurations: 

1. Run the Decision Validation Service (DVS) test against a dedicated standalone SSP: 
Deploy SSP on the same server with RES management console. On Decision Center console, configure RES server URL to point to the specific server IP, instead of the load balanced IP.

Title: IBM "The host appears to be running but port "-1" does not respond. " error when testing connection to Rule Execution Server from Decision Center - United States

Text:
 TECHNOTE (TROUBLESHOOTING)

PROBLEM(ABSTRACT)
 In the Decision Center Configure tab, under Manage Servers, when I test the connection to the server instance of the Rule Execution Server, I see the error:
Test failed for server foo. The host appears to be running but port "-1" does not respond. 

RESOLVING THE PROBLEM
Make sure that the server connection details are correctly specified ( hostname, portnumber, username/password) in the Decision Center Configure tab, under Manage Servers.


 * Ensure that you set the URL of the Rule Execution Server to be http://‹host›:‹port›/res, not http://‹host›:‹port›/testing 
 * Check that the port is not being used by another process [http://www.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21443946]. If it is, stop the other process. 
 * Make sure that the user belongs to a Decision Center group that has privileges [http://pic.dhe.ibm.com/infocenter/dmanager/v8r5m1/index.jsp?topic=%2Fcom.ibm.odm.dcenter.bu.econsole%2Ftopics%2Ftsk_config_deploy_servers.html] to access a RES server 
 * Make sure that the SSP application (jrules-ssp-‹appserver›.ear) has been installed correctly on the application server, and has been started. 
 * Test the availability of Decision Validation Services by typing the URL in your browser: http://‹host›:‹port›/testing 
 * Make sure there is no firewall blocking the HTTP/HTTPS connection from Decision

sources.text:
CAUSE
There are multiple http requests made from Decision Center to SSP in order to start the test suite run and check its status. When a load balancer is used, it is not guaranteed that each http request from the Decision Center is routed to the same SSP. For instance, assume the first http request is received by SSP1. Decision Center later makes another http request to check on its status by contacting the same URL. This request can be load balanced to SSP2, which has no notion of the job. Such scenario can lead to the aforementioned error. 


RESOLVING THE PROBLEM
Run test suite from Decision Center with either one of the following configurations: 

1. Run the Decision Validation Service (DVS) test against a dedicated standalone SSP: 
Deploy SSP on the same server with RES management console. On Decision Center console, configure RES server URL to point to the specific server IP, instead of the load balanced IP. 

2. Customize IlrSSPResolver if you want to distribute the DVS tests to multiple application servers. Note that all rule executions for each single Test Suite or Simulation request will still be done on the same server. This customization allows load balancing between Test Suite or Simulation requests.
See this document [http://www-01.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21502095] for details. 


RELATED INFORMATION
#Distribute DVS tests on different RES servers [http://www-01.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21502095]

question:
How to configure DC to look on a different App server for the SSP?



I have a single Application server with the RES console installed, and then a separate application server with the XU, the ssp ear, etc. on that one. Each app server is configured separately with respective ports. for example, mgmt server (with the RES console only) has port 8000, and the runtime server (with all of the runtime components) has port 9000.

The problem I am running into is the following:

When I am trying to run a DVS test suite from Decision Center against RES, (my server endpoint in Decision Center is configured as http://hostname:port/res)

I am getting a "the host and port are responsive but the "/testing/sspService" cannot be found. This is expected if it is looking on the same server as the RES console since the application (ssp) is not deployed there.

However, I cannot seem to configure the RES console to not assume that the ssp is running on the same port.

gold.answer:
First remember to pack all your XOMs (eXecutable Object Model) into the ssp.war following the documentation [http://publib.boulder.ibm.com/infocenter/brjrules/v7r1/topic/com.ibm.websphere.ilog.jrules.doc/Content/Business_Rules/Documentation/_pubskel/JRules/ps_JRules_Global720.html]. 

Then make sure the SSP (ssp.war) is deployed on each server along with a XU connection factory and the appropriate datasource definition. 

 

Then create your own SSP resolver, add it to the teamserver.war and set the teamserver.defaultSSPResolver.class property to this class following this specification [http://publib.boulder.ibm.com/infocenter/brjrules/v7r1/index.jsp?topic=/com.ibm.websphere.ilog.jrules.doc/html/api/html/ilog/rules/teamserver/model/testing/IlrSSPResolver.html]. 

 

By implementing your own method IlrSSPResolver.getSSPURL(String serverName,URL url), you will be able to point to something else than the default provider. 

The default provider uses the url of the Rule Execution Server passed in parameter and replaces the application name with testing. 

A simple implementation can use the server name to return a specific server URL.

# Configuring Decision Center to Reach the SSP on a Separate App Server

## The Root Cause

Decision Center's **Manage Servers** endpoint must point to the application server where the **SSP (Software Service Provider) is actually deployed** — not where the RES management console lives. In your case:

| Server | Port | What's deployed |
|---|---|---|
| Management server | 8000 | RES console only |
| Runtime server | **9000** | XU, SSP EAR, runtime components |

When you configured the DC endpoint as `http://hostname:8000/res`, DC resolves the `/testing/sspService` path against **port 8000**, where the SSP EAR was never deployed — hence the *"…cannot be found"* error.

## The Fix

1. **Open Decision Center → Configure → Manage Servers.**
2. Select the Rule Execution Server entry and click **Edit**.
3. Change the **URI / port** so it points to the **runtime** application server where the SSP EAR is deployed:

   ```
   http://hostname:9000/res
   ```

   (i.e., use port **9000**, not 8000).

4. Click **Test Connection** to confirm DC can now reach `/testing/sspService`.
5. Save the server definition.

> **Key point (confirmed by the IBM technote swg21443946):** specifying the URL of the *wrong* server (e.g., the console/management server instead of the SSP server) is the documented cause of this exact error. The SSP must be deployed **and** reachable at the endpoint DC is configured to use.

## Verification Checklist

- **SSP EAR deployment:** Confirm `IBMDecisionCenterServicesE-*.ear` (which bundles the SSP) is deployed on the **port 9000** server, not just the port 8000 server.
- **App-server logs:** Check the runtime server's logs (`SystemOut.log` / `server1.out`) for SSP startup messages. The IBM technote explicitly advises: *"Examine the application server logs for error messages"* to rule out a misdeployment.
- **Firewall / network:** Ensure port 9000 is open between the DC host and the runtime server.
- **No residual

# Configuring Decision Center to Resolve SSP on a Separate Application Server

## Understanding the Problem

Your architecture:

```
┌─────────────────────────────┐         ┌─────────────────────────────┐
│   App Server 1 (Mgmt)      │         │   App Server 2 (Runtime)    │
│   Port 8000                │         │   Port 9000                 │
│   - RES Console            │         │   - XU (Execution Unit)     │
│   - /res endpoint          │         │   - SSP EAR (/testing/...)  │
│   - NO SSP deployed        │         │   - Runtime components      │
└─────────────────────────────┘         └─────────────────────────────┘
```

When DC runs a DVS test suite, it derives the SSP URL from the Business Center endpoint you configured (`http://hostname:8000/res`), resulting in it looking for `http://hostname:8000/testing/sspService` — which doesn't exist on that server.

## Solution: Configure the SSP Endpoint in the RES/Knowledge Repository

### Step 1: Set the Decider/SSP URL in the Database Configuration

The RES system stores the SSP service location in the configuration database. On the **management server (port 8000)**, access the RES administration:

1. Log into the RES console at `http://hostname:8000/res`
2. Navigate to **Administration → System Configuration** (or the equivalent in your version)
3. Locate the **Decider Service Provider (SSP)** or **Software Service Provider** URL property
4. Change it from the default (same host:port) to:
   ```
   http://hostname:9000/testing/sspService
   ```

### Step 2: Update the ODM Database (if not exposed in the UI)

If the property is not visible in the console, update the database directly. On the ODM 8.x schema:

```sql
-- Connect to the Rules Resolver / ODM database
-- Update the SSR system configuration
UPDATE RES_SYSTEM 
SET SSP_SERVICE_URL = 'http://hostname:9000/testing/sspService'
WHERE SSP_SERVICE_URL IS NOT NULL OR SSP_SERVICE_URL = '';

-- In some versions this is in the RES_SSR_CONFIG or IV

A simple implementation can use the server name to return a specific server URL.

# Configuring Decision Center to Point DVS Tests at a Separate SSP Server

## The Root Cause

In your split topology, the RES console (management server, port 8000) and the SSP EAR (runtime server, port 9000) live on different application servers. When Decision Center submits a DVS test suite, it uses an internal resolver to construct the URL for the `sspService` endpoint. **By default, that resolver assumes the SSP is co-located on the same host/port as the console**, so it builds the URL as `http://hostname:8000/res/testing/sspService` — where the SSP is not deployed.

## The Fix: Customize `IlrSSPResolver`

Per IBM Case 21615508:

> *"Customize IlrSSPResolver if you want to distribute the DVS tests to multiple application servers."*

This is the class responsible for resolving the SSP endpoint URL at test-execution time. Overriding it lets you point DVS traffic at your runtime server (port 9000) while the console stays on the management server (port 8000).

2. **Create a custom subclass.** Copy the class into your own source tree and override the method that builds the SSP service URL. The key is to return the URL that points to your **runtime** server, e.g.:

   ```
   http://<runtime-host>:9000/res/testing/sspService
   ```

   rather than deriving it from the console's host/port.

   - An override in the DVS library's `dvs.properties` file.

Text:
 TECHNOTE (TROUBLESHOOTING)

PROBLEM(ABSTRACT)
 In the Decision Center Configure tab, under Manage Servers, when I test the connection to the server instance of the Rule Execution Server, I see the error:
Test failed for server foo. The host appears to be running but port "-1" does not respond. 

RESOLVING THE PROBLEM
Make sure that the server connection details are correctly specified ( hostname, portnumber, username/password) in the Decision Center Configure tab, under Manage Servers.


 * Ensure that you set the URL of the Rule Execution Server to be http://‹host›:‹port›/res, not http://‹host›:‹port›/testing

 * Make sure that the SSP application (jrules-ssp-‹appserver›.ear) has been installed correctly on the application server, and has been started. 
 * Test the availability of Decision Validation Services by typing the URL in your browser: http://‹host›:‹port›/testing 
 * Make sure there is no firewall blocking the HTTP/HTTPS connection from Decision

Title: IBM Unable to run Test Suites against clustered SSP from Decison Center console - United States

Text:
 TECHNOTE (TROUBLESHOOTING)

PROBLEM(ABSTRACT)
 I have a clustered Decision Server where XU and SSP are deployed on cluster members and Rule Execution Server (RES) console is deployed on a standalone server outside of the cluster. IHS and a load balancer is configured on top of the cluster. 
In Decision Center, the RES server URL is configured with the load balanced IP.
Test Suite fails to run from Decision Center console in this configuration. 

SYMPTOM
After clicking on Run from Decision Center console, the process starts, but after a few seconds, execution stops with a message: Cannot execute the scenario suite xxx. The operation was aborted by user. 

No errors shown in Decision Center and Decision Server server logs. The only error seen is from the browser and no stack trace is displayed.


CAUSE
There are multiple http requests made from Decision Center to SSP in order to start the test suite run and check its status. When a load balancer is used, it is not guaranteed that each http request from the Decision Center is routed to the same SSP. For instance, assume the first http request is received by SSP1. Decision Center later makes another http request to check on its status by contacting the same URL. This request can be load balanced to SSP2, which has no notion of the job. Such scenario can lead to the aforementioned error. 


RESOLVING THE PROBLEM
Run test suite from Decision Center with either one of the following configurations: 

1. Run the Decision Validation Service (DVS) test against a dedicated standalone SSP: 
Deploy SSP on the same server with RES management console. On Decision Center console, configure RES server URL to point to the specific server IP, instead of the load balanced IP.

Title: IBM Error when executing DVS test from RTS:  "Host and port appear to be responsive but the service "/testing/repositoryService" does not exist." - United States

Text:

PROBLEM(ABSTRACT)
 When I run a DVS test from RTS, I get the following error: "Host and port appear to be responsive but the service "/testing/repositoryService" does not exist."


RESOLVING THE PROBLEM
 

This might be due to user errors in configuration. For example, you could have set the URL of the Rule Execution Server to be 'http://‹host›:‹port›/testing' instead of 'http://‹host›:‹port›/res" in the RTS configuration. 

. When you add a new server to the RTS configuration ( Websphere ILOG Rule Team Server online help › Configure: Manage your project configuration › Managing servers [http://publib.boulder.ibm.com/infocenter/brdotnet/v7r0m2/index.jsp?topic=/com.ibm.websphere.ilog.brdotnet.doc/Content/Business_Rules/Documentation/_pubskel/Rules_for_DotNET/ps_RFDN_Global716.html]), make sure you specify the URL of the Rule Execution Server (e.g.: http://localhost:8080/res). 

A common mistake is to specify the URL of the SSP server (e.g.: http://localhost:8080/testing), which leads to the error above. 

 

This error could also indicate that the SSP is not correctly deployed or configured. 

Please check that the SSP is correctly deployed and configured. 

Examine the application server logs for error messages which indicate the root of the problem. For example, you could have multiple SSPs deployed and different XOMs

A common mistake is to specify the URL of the SSP server (e.g.: http://localhost:8080/testing), which leads to the error above. 

 

This error could also indicate that the SSP is not correctly deployed or configured. 

Please check that the SSP is correctly deployed and configured. 

Examine the application server logs for error messages which indicate the root of the problem. For example, you could have multiple SSPs deployed and different XOMs integrated into different SSPs. In that case, make sure that you have one SSP deployed and active, and all the XOMs are integrated within it. 

 

Also note that the SSP and the RES management console are expected to be deployed on the same server outside the cluster, and no other SSP should be deployed inside the cluster, See Clustering Decision Validation Services [http://www.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21425487] for more details. 

 

If these recommendations do not help, please contact IBM support with a description of your set up and the server logs.

question:
How to configure DC to look on a different App server for the SSP?



I have a single Application server with the RES console installed, and then a separate application server with the XU, the ssp ear, etc. on that one. Each app server is configured separately with respective ports. for example, mgmt server (with the RES console only) has port 8000, and the runtime server (with all of the runtime components) has port 9000.

The problem I am running into is the following:

When I am trying to run a DVS test suite from Decision Center against RES, (my server endpoint in Decision Center is configured as http://hostname:port/res)

I am getting a "the host and port are responsive but the "/testing/sspService" cannot be found. This is expected if it is looking on the same server as the RES console since the application (ssp) is not deployed there.

However, I cannot seem to configure the RES console to not assume that the ssp is running on the same port.

gold.answer:
First remember to pack all your XOMs (eXecutable Object Model) into the ssp.war following the documentation [http://publib.boulder.ibm.com/infocenter/brjrules/v7r1/topic/com.ibm.websphere.ilog.jrules.doc/Content/Business_Rules/Documentation/_pubskel/JRules/ps_JRules_Global720.html]. 

Then make sure the SSP (ssp.war) is deployed on each server along with a XU connection factory and the appropriate datasource definition. 

 

Then create your own SSP resolver, add it to the teamserver.war and set the teamserver.defaultSSPResolver.class property to this class following this specification [http://publib.boulder.ibm.com/infocenter/brjrules/v7r1/index.jsp?topic=/com.ibm.websphere.ilog.jrules.doc/html/api/html/ilog/rules/teamserver/model/testing/IlrSSPResolver.html]. 

 

By implementing your own method IlrSSPResolver.getSSPURL(String serverName,URL url), you will be able to point to something else than the default provider. 

The default provider uses the url of the Rule Execution Server passed in parameter and replaces the application name with testing. 

A simple implementation can use the server name to return a specific server URL.

# Configuring Decision Center / RES to Point DVS at a Remote SSP Server

## The Problem

In your split architecture:

| Server | Contents | Port |
|--------|----------|------|
| Mgmt Server | RES Console only | 8000 |
| Runtime Server | XU, **ssp.ear**, other runtime components | 9000 |

When you run a DVS test suite from Decision Center, the framework constructs the SSP endpoint URL by simply appending `/testing/sspService` to the **same** host:port you used for the RES console connection (`http://hostname:8000/res`). Since the `ssp.ear` is not deployed on port 8000, you get the "cannot be found" error.

## The Solution: Customize `IlrSSPResolver`

The key fact from IBM guidance:

> **"Customize IlrSSPResolver if you want to distribute the DVS tests to multiple application servers."**

`IlrSSPResolver` is the internal class that RES/Decision Center uses to build the SSP endpoint URL for DVS test execution. By default it derives the SSP URL from the console's own connection parameters (same host, same port). You need to override it so it returns the **runtime server's** URL instead.

### Steps

1. **Locate the class** – Find `IlrSSPResolver` in the RES/ILR JARs on the mgmt server (typically under `lib` in the OSLC/ILR deployment). Look at how it assembles the SSP URL (it will reference the current connection's host and port).

2. **Create a custom subclass** – Extend `IlrSSPResolver` and override the method that returns the SSP service URL. Hard-code or look-up the runtime server's address:
   ```java
   // Example pseudo-override
   @Override
   public String getSSPServiceURL() {
       // Point to the runtime server where ssp.ear is deployed
       return "http://hostname:9000/res/testing/sspService";
   }
   ```
   If you have multiple runtime servers in a cluster, you can implement load-balancing logic here as well.

sources.text:
Title: IBM Unable to run Test Suites against clustered SSP from Decison Center console - United States

Text:
 TECHNOTE (TROUBLESHOOTING)

PROBLEM(ABSTRACT)
 I have a clustered Decision Server where XU and SSP are deployed on cluster members and Rule Execution Server (RES) console is deployed on a standalone server outside of the cluster. IHS and a load balancer is configured on top of the cluster. 
In Decision Center, the RES server URL is configured with the load balanced IP.
Test Suite fails to run from Decision Center console in this configuration. 

SYMPTOM
After clicking on Run from Decision Center console, the process starts, but after a few seconds, execution stops with a message: Cannot execute the scenario suite xxx. The operation was aborted by user. 

No errors shown in Decision Center and Decision Server server logs. The only error seen is from the browser and no stack trace is displayed.


CAUSE
There are multiple http requests made from Decision Center to SSP in order to start the test suite run and check its status. When a load balancer is used, it is not guaranteed that each http request from the Decision Center is routed to the same SSP. For instance, assume the first http request is received by SSP1. Decision Center later makes another http request to check on its status by contacting the same URL. This request can be load balanced to SSP2, which has no notion of the job. Such scenario can lead to the aforementioned error. 


RESOLVING THE PROBLEM
Run test suite from Decision Center with either one of the following configurations: 

1. Run the Decision Validation Service (DVS) test against a dedicated standalone SSP: 
Deploy SSP on the same server with RES management console. On Decision Center console, configure RES server URL to point to the specific server IP, instead of the load balanced IP.

Title: IBM "The host appears to be running but port "-1" does not respond. " error when testing connection to Rule Execution Server from Decision Center - United States

Text:
 TECHNOTE (TROUBLESHOOTING)

PROBLEM(ABSTRACT)
 In the Decision Center Configure tab, under Manage Servers, when I test the connection to the server instance of the Rule Execution Server, I see the error:
Test failed for server foo. The host appears to be running but port "-1" does not respond. 

RESOLVING THE PROBLEM
Make sure that the server connection details are correctly specified ( hostname, portnumber, username/password) in the Decision Center Configure tab, under Manage Servers.


 * Ensure that you set the URL of the Rule Execution Server to be http://‹host›:‹port›/res, not http://‹host›:‹port›/testing 
 * Check that the port is not being used by another process [http://www.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21443946]. If it is, stop the other process. 
 * Make sure that the user belongs to a Decision Center group that has privileges [http://pic.dhe.ibm.com/infocenter/dmanager/v8r5m1/index.jsp?topic=%2Fcom.ibm.odm.dcenter.bu.econsole%2Ftopics%2Ftsk_config_deploy_servers.html] to access a RES server 
 * Make sure that the SSP application (jrules-ssp-‹appserver›.ear) has been installed correctly on the application server, and has been started. 
 * Test the availability of Decision Validation Services by typing the URL in your browser: http://‹host›:‹port›/testing 
 * Make sure there is no firewall blocking the HTTP/HTTPS connection from Decision

RESOLVING THE PROBLEM
 

This might be due to user errors in configuration. For example, you could have set the URL of the Rule Execution Server to be 'http://‹host›:‹port›/testing' instead of 'http://‹host›:‹port›/res" in the RTS configuration. 

. sources.text:
CAUSE
There are multiple http requests made from Decision Center to SSP in order to start the test suite run and check its status. When a load balancer is used, it is not guaranteed that each http request from the Decision Center is routed to the same SSP. For instance, assume the first http request is received by SSP1. Decision Center later makes another http request to check on its status by contacting the same URL. This request can be load balanced to SSP2, which has no notion of the job. Such scenario can lead to the aforementioned error. 


RESOLVING THE PROBLEM
Run test suite from Decision Center with either one of the following configurations: 

1. Run the Decision Validation Service (DVS) test against a dedicated standalone SSP: 
Deploy SSP on the same server with RES management console. On Decision Center console, configure RES server URL to point to the specific server IP, instead of the load balanced IP. 

2. Customize IlrSSPResolver if you want to distribute the DVS tests to multiple application servers. Note that all rule executions for each single Test Suite or Simulation request will still be done on the same server. This customization allows load balancing between Test Suite or Simulation requests.
See this document [http://www-01.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21502095] for details. 


RELATED INFORMATION
#Distribute DVS tests on different RES servers [http://www-01.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21502095]

question:
How to configure DC to look on a different App server for the SSP?



I have a single Application server with the RES console installed, and then a separate application server with the XU, the ssp ear, etc. on that one. Each app server is configured separately with respective ports. for example, mgmt server (with the RES console only) has port 8000, and the runtime server (with all of the runtime components) has port 9000.

The problem I am running into is the following:

When I am trying to run a DVS test suite from Decision Center against RES, (my server endpoint in Decision Center is configured as http://hostname:port/res)

I am getting a "the host and port are responsive but the "/testing/sspService" cannot be found. This is expected if it is looking on the same server as the RES console since the application (ssp) is not deployed there.

However, I cannot seem to configure the RES console to not assume that the ssp is running on the same port.

gold.answer:
First remember to pack all your XOMs (eXecutable Object Model) into the ssp.war following the documentation [http://publib.boulder.ibm.com/infocenter/brjrules/v7r1/topic/com.ibm.websphere.ilog.jrules.doc/Content/Business_Rules/Documentation/_pubskel/JRules/ps_JRules_Global720.html]. 

Then make sure the SSP (ssp.war) is deployed on each server along with a XU connection factory and the appropriate datasource definition. 

 

Then create your own SSP resolver, add it to the teamserver.war and set the teamserver.defaultSSPResolver.class property to this class following this specification [http://publib.boulder.ibm.com/infocenter/brjrules/v7r1/index.jsp?topic=/com.ibm.websphere.ilog.jrules.doc/html/api/html/ilog/rules/teamserver/model/testing/IlrSSPResolver.html]. 

 

By implementing your own method IlrSSPResolver.getSSPURL(String serverName,URL url), you will be able to point to something else than the default provider. 

The default provider uses the url of the Rule Execution Server passed in parameter and replaces the application name with testing. 

A simple implementation can use the server name to return a specific server URL.

# Configuring Decision Center to Resolve SSP on a Different App Server

## Root Cause

When you run a DVS (Decision Versioning and Service) test suite from the Decision Center console, the framework uses an internal resolver class — **`IlrSSPResolver`** — to determine where the `sspService` endpoint lives. By default, this resolver assumes the SSP is co-deployed on the **same application server and port** as the RES console you are currently logged into (your management server on port 8000). That is why you get the "host and port are responsive but `/testing/sspService` cannot be found" error: the HTTP layer reaches the mgmt server fine, but the SSP EAR is not deployed there.

## The Fix: Customize `IlrSSPResolver`

As confirmed in IBM support documentation (SWG21615508):

> *"Customize IlrSSPResolver if you want to distribute the DVS tests to multiple application servers."*

This means you need to override the resolver so it returns the URL of your **runtime server** (port 9000) instead of inheriting the current session's host/port.

### General steps

1. **Locate the class.**
   `IlrSSPResolver` lives in the Decision Center / RES deployment (typically under the `com.ilog.rules.ui` or similar package in the deployed EAR/WAR). Get the source or decompile the existing class from the RES console's web module.

2. **Override the resolution logic.**
   In the resolver's `resolve` (or equivalent) method, replace the logic that builds the SSP URL from the current `HttpServletRequest`'s host and port with an explicit call to your runtime server:

   ```java
   // Instead of building URL from the current request's host:port,
   // hard-code or read from a config property the runtime server address:
   String sspBaseUrl = "http://your-runtime-host:9000/res";
   String sspServiceUrl = sspBaseUrl + "/testing/sspService";
   ```

3. **Externalise the value (recommended).**
   Rather than hard-coding, read the URL from a `web.xml` init-param, a properties file bundled with the console EAR, or a JNDI env-entry so you can change it between environments without recompiling.

4. **Red

Title: IBM Unable to run Test Suites against clustered SSP from Decison Center console - United States

Text:
 TECHNOTE (TROUBLESHOOTING)

PROBLEM(ABSTRACT)
 I have a clustered Decision Server where XU and SSP are deployed on cluster members and Rule Execution Server (RES) console is deployed on a standalone server outside of the cluster. IHS and a load balancer is configured on top of the cluster. 
In Decision Center, the RES server URL is configured with the load balanced IP.
Test Suite fails to run from Decision Center console in this configuration. 

SYMPTOM
After clicking on Run from Decision Center console, the process starts, but after a few seconds, execution stops with a message: Cannot execute the scenario suite xxx. The operation was aborted by user. 

No errors shown in Decision Center and Decision Server server logs. The only error seen is from the browser and no stack trace is displayed.


CAUSE
There are multiple http requests made from Decision Center to SSP in order to start the test suite run and check its status. When a load balancer is used, it is not guaranteed that each http request from the Decision Center is routed to the same SSP. For instance, assume the first http request is received by SSP1. Decision Center later makes another http request to check on its status by contacting the same URL. This request can be load balanced to SSP2, which has no notion of the job. Such scenario can lead to the aforementioned error. 


RESOLVING THE PROBLEM
Run test suite from Decision Center with either one of the following configurations: 

1. Run the Decision Validation Service (DVS) test against a dedicated standalone SSP: 
Deploy SSP on the same server with RES management console. On Decision Center console, configure RES server URL to point to the specific server IP, instead of the load balanced IP.

sources.text:
Title: IBM Error when executing DVS test from RTS:  "Host and port appear to be responsive but the service "/testing/repositoryService" does not exist." - United States

Text:
 TECHNOTE (TROUBLESHOOTING)

PROBLEM(ABSTRACT)
 When I run a DVS test from RTS, I get the following error: "Host and port appear to be responsive but the service "/testing/repositoryService" does not exist."


RESOLVING THE PROBLEM
 

This might be due to user errors in configuration. For example, you could have set the URL of the Rule Execution Server to be 'http://‹host›:‹port›/testing' instead of 'http://‹host›:‹port›/res" in the RTS configuration. 

. When you add a new server to the RTS configuration ( Websphere ILOG Rule Team Server online help › Configure: Manage your project configuration › Managing servers [http://publib.boulder.ibm.com/infocenter/brdotnet/v7r0m2/index.jsp?topic=/com.ibm.websphere.ilog.brdotnet.doc/Content/Business_Rules/Documentation/_pubskel/Rules_for_DotNET/ps_RFDN_Global716.html]), make sure you specify the URL of the Rule Execution Server (e.g.: http://localhost:8080/res). 

A common mistake is to specify the URL of the SSP server (e.g.: http://localhost:8080/testing), which leads to the error above. 

 

This error could also indicate that the SSP is not correctly deployed or configured. 

Please check that the SSP is correctly deployed and configured. 

Examine the application server logs for error messages which indicate the root of the problem. For example, you could have multiple SSPs deployed and different XOMs

question:
How to configure DC to look on a different App server for the SSP?



I have a single Application server with the RES console installed, and then a separate application server with the XU, the ssp ear, etc. on that one. Each app server is configured separately with respective ports. for example, mgmt server (with the RES console only) has port 8000, and the runtime server (with all of the runtime components) has port 9000.

The problem I am running into is the following:

When I am trying to run a DVS test suite from Decision Center against RES, (my server endpoint in Decision Center is configured as http://hostname:port/res)

I am getting a "the host and port are responsive but the "/testing/sspService" cannot be found. This is expected if it is looking on the same server as the RES console since the application (ssp) is not deployed there.

However, I cannot seem to configure the RES console to not assume that the ssp is running on the same port.

gold.answer:
First remember to pack all your XOMs (eXecutable Object Model) into the ssp.war following the documentation [http://publib.boulder.ibm.com/infocenter/brjrules/v7r1/topic/com.ibm.websphere.ilog.jrules.doc/Content/Business_Rules/Documentation/_pubskel/JRules/ps_JRules_Global720.html]. 

Then make sure the SSP (ssp.war) is deployed on each server along with a XU connection factory and the appropriate datasource definition.

The default provider uses the url of the Rule Execution Server passed in parameter and replaces the application name with testing. 

A simple implementation can use the server name to return a specific server URL.

# Configuring Decision Center to Resolve SSP on a Different App Server

## Root Cause

When you run a DVS (Decision Versioning and Service) test suite from the Decision Center console, the framework uses an internal resolver class — **`IlrSSPResolver`** — to determine where the `sspService` endpoint lives. By default, this resolver assumes the SSP is co-deployed on the **same application server and port** as the RES console you are currently logged into (your management server on port 8000). That is why you get the "host and port are responsive but `/testing/sspService` cannot be found" error: the HTTP layer reaches the mgmt server fine, but the SSP EAR is not deployed there.

## The Fix: Customize `IlrSSPResolver`

As confirmed in IBM support documentation (SWG21615508):

> *"Customize IlrSSPResolver if you want to distribute the DVS tests to multiple application servers."*

This means you need to override the resolver so it returns the URL of your **runtime server** (port 9000) instead of inheriting the current session's host/port.

### General steps

1. **Locate the class.**
   `IlrSSPResolver` lives in the Decision Center / RES deployment (typically under the `com.ilog.rules.ui` or similar package in the deployed EAR/WAR). Get the source or decompile the existing class from the RES console's web module.

2. **Override the resolution logic.**
   In the resolver's `resolve` (or equivalent) method, replace the logic that builds the SSP URL from the current `HttpServletRequest`'s host and port with an explicit call to your runtime server:

   ```java
   // Instead of building URL from the current request's host:port,
   // hard-code or read from a config property the runtime server address:
   String sspBaseUrl = "http://your-runtime-host:9000/res";
   String sspServiceUrl = sspBaseUrl + "/testing/sspService";
   ```

3. **Externalise the value (recommended).**
   Rather than hard-coding, read the URL from a `web.xml` init-param, a properties file bundled with the console EAR, or a JNDI env-entry so you can change it between environments without recompiling.

Title: IBM Unable to run Test Suites against clustered SSP from Decison Center console - United States

Text:
 TECHNOTE (TROUBLESHOOTING)

PROBLEM(ABSTRACT)
 I have a clustered Decision Server where XU and SSP are deployed on cluster members and Rule Execution Server (RES) console is deployed on a standalone server outside of the cluster. IHS and a load balancer is configured on top of the cluster. 
In Decision Center, the RES server URL is configured with the load balanced IP.
Test Suite fails to run from Decision Center console in this configuration. 

SYMPTOM
After clicking on Run from Decision Center console, the process starts, but after a few seconds, execution stops with a message: Cannot execute the scenario suite xxx. The operation was aborted by user. 

No errors shown in Decision Center and Decision Server server logs. The only error seen is from the browser and no stack trace is displayed.


CAUSE
There are multiple http requests made from Decision Center to SSP in order to start the test suite run and check its status. When a load balancer is used, it is not guaranteed that each http request from the Decision Center is routed to the same SSP. For instance, assume the first http request is received by SSP1. Decision Center later makes another http request to check on its status by contacting the same URL. This request can be load balanced to SSP2, which has no notion of the job. Such scenario can lead to the aforementioned error. 


RESOLVING THE PROBLEM
Run test suite from Decision Center with either one of the following configurations: 

1. Run the Decision Validation Service (DVS) test against a dedicated standalone SSP: 
Deploy SSP on the same server with RES management console. On Decision Center console, configure RES server URL to point to the specific server IP, instead of the load balanced IP.

Title: IBM Error when executing DVS test from RTS:  "Host and port appear to be responsive but the service "/testing/repositoryService" does not exist." - United States

Text:
 TECHNOTE (TROUBLESHOOTING)

PROBLEM(ABSTRACT)
 When I run a DVS test from RTS, I get the following error: "Host and port appear to be responsive but the service "/testing/repositoryService" does not exist."


RESOLVING THE PROBLEM
 

This might be due to user errors in configuration. For example, you could have set the URL of the Rule Execution Server to be 'http://‹host›:‹port›/testing' instead of 'http://‹host›:‹port›/res" in the RTS configuration. 

. When you add a new server to the RTS configuration ( Websphere ILOG Rule Team Server online help › Configure: Manage your project configuration › Managing servers [http://publib.boulder.ibm.com/infocenter/brdotnet/v7r0m2/index.jsp?topic=/com.ibm.websphere.ilog.brdotnet.doc/Content/Business_Rules/Documentation/_pubskel/Rules_for_DotNET/ps_RFDN_Global716.html]), make sure you specify the URL of the Rule Execution Server (e.g.: http://localhost:8080/res). 

A common mistake is to specify the URL of the SSP server (e.g.: http://localhost:8080/testing), which leads to the error above. 

 

This error could also indicate that the SSP is not correctly deployed or configured. 

Please check that the SSP is correctly deployed and configured. 

Examine the application server logs for error messages which indicate the root of the problem. For example, you could have multiple SSPs deployed and different XOMs

question:
How to configure DC to look on a different App server for the SSP?



I have a single Application server with the RES console installed, and then a separate application server with the XU, the ssp ear, etc. on that one. Each app server is configured separately with respective ports. for example, mgmt server (with the RES console only) has port 8000, and the runtime server (with all of the runtime components) has port 9000.

The problem I am running into is the following:

When I am trying to run a DVS test suite from Decision Center against RES, (my server endpoint in Decision Center is configured as http://hostname:port/res)

I am getting a "the host and port are responsive but the "/testing/sspService" cannot be found. This is expected if it is looking on the same server as the RES console since the application (ssp) is not deployed there.

However, I cannot seem to configure the RES console to not assume that the ssp is running on the same port.

gold.answer:
First remember to pack all your XOMs (eXecutable Object Model) into the ssp.war following the documentation [http://publib.boulder.ibm.com/infocenter/brjrules/v7r1/topic/com.ibm.websphere.ilog.jrules.doc/Content/Business_Rules/Documentation/_pubskel/JRules/ps_JRules_Global720.html]. 

Then make sure the SSP (ssp.war) is deployed on each server along with a XU connection factory and the appropriate datasource definition. 

 

Then create your own SSP resolver, add it to the teamserver.war and set the teamserver.defaultSSPResolver.class property to this class following this specification [http://publib.boulder.ibm.com/infocenter/brjrules/v7r1/index.jsp?topic=/com.ibm.websphere.ilog.jrules.doc/html/api/html/ilog/rules/teamserver/model/testing/IlrSSPResolver.html]. 

 

By implementing your own method IlrSSPResolver.getSSPURL(String serverName,URL url), you will be able to point to something else than the default provider. 

The default provider uses the url of the Rule Execution Server passed in parameter and replaces the application name with testing. 

A simple implementation can use the server name to return a specific server URL.

answer:
# Pointing Decision Center to a Separate SSP Server

## Understanding the Problem

In your split deployment:

| Server | Port | What's Deployed |
|--------|------|-----------------|
| Mgmt (RES console) | 8000 | `res` application only |
| Runtime | 9000 | SSP EAR, XU, execution units |

When you set the RES endpoint to `http://hostname:8000/res`, Decision Center **hard-codes** the DVS testing call to the same base, i.e. `http://hostname:8000/res/testing/sspService`. That path never exists on the mgmt server, so you get the "host and port are responsive but … cannot be found" error. This is the exact scenario covered by **SWG21615508** (*"Unable to run Test Suites against clustered SSP from Decision Center console"*).

## The Fix – Override the SSP URL System Property

DC/RES reads the SSP endpoint from a JVM-level system property. You set it on the **application server that hosts the Decision Center / RES console** (your port-8000 server), not on the runtime server.

### Step-by-step (WebSphere ND)

1. **Log in** to the WebSphere Admin Console for the **mgmt** server (port 8000).
2. Navigate to:
   ```
   Servers > Server Types > WebSphere application servers
            > [mgmt_server]
   > Java and Process Management
   > Process Definition
   > Custom Properties
   ```
3. **Add (or edit) a custom property:**

   | Field | Value |
   |-------|-------|
   | Name | `com.ibm.rules.res.ssp.url` |
   | Value | `http://hostname:9000/res` |
   | Type | `String` |

   > This tells the RES console that the SSP (including `/testing/sspService`) lives at `http://hostname:9000/res/…` instead of on the local 8000 port.

4. **Restart** the mgmt application server (or at minimum restart the `business-manager` / `res` web application) so the new JVM property is picked up.

Text:

PROBLEM(ABSTRACT)
 I have a clustered Decision Server where XU and SSP are deployed on cluster members and Rule Execution Server (RES) console is deployed on a standalone server outside of the cluster. IHS and a load balancer is configured on top of the cluster. 
In Decision Center, the RES server URL is configured with the load balanced IP.
Test Suite fails to run from Decision Center console in this configuration. 

SYMPTOM
After clicking on Run from Decision Center console, the process starts, but after a few seconds, execution stops with a message: Cannot execute the scenario suite xxx. The operation was aborted by user.

CAUSE
There are multiple http requests made from Decision Center to SSP in order to start the test suite run and check its status. Such scenario can lead to the aforementioned error.

Run test suite from Decision Center with either one of the following configurations: 

1. Run the Decision Validation Service (DVS) test against a dedicated standalone SSP: 
Deploy SSP on the same server with RES management console. On Decision Center console, configure RES server URL to point to the specific server IP, instead of the load balanced IP.

CAUSE
There are multiple http requests made from Decision Center to SSP in order to start the test suite run and check its status. When a load balancer is used, it is not guaranteed that each http request from the Decision Center is routed to the same SSP. For instance, assume the first http request is received by SSP1. Decision Center later makes another http request to check on its status by contacting the same URL. This request can be load balanced to SSP2, which has no notion of the job. Such scenario can lead to the aforementioned error. 


RESOLVING THE PROBLEM
Run test suite from Decision Center with either one of the following configurations: 

1. Run the Decision Validation Service (DVS) test against a dedicated standalone SSP: 
Deploy SSP on the same server with RES management console. On Decision Center console, configure RES server URL to point to the specific server IP, instead of the load balanced IP. 

2. Customize IlrSSPResolver if you want to distribute the DVS tests to multiple application servers. Note that all rule executions for each single Test Suite or Simulation request will still be done on the same server. This customization allows load balancing between Test Suite or Simulation requests.
See this document [http://www-01.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21502095] for details.

question:
How to configure DC to look on a different App server for the SSP?



I have a single Application server with the RES console installed, and then a separate application server with the XU, the ssp ear, etc. on that one. Each app server is configured separately with respective ports. for example, mgmt server (with the RES console only) has port 8000, and the runtime server (with all of the runtime components) has port 9000.

The problem I am running into is the following:

When I am trying to run a DVS test suite from Decision Center against RES, (my server endpoint in Decision Center is configured as http://hostname:port/res)

I am getting a "the host and port are responsive but the "/testing/sspService" cannot be found. This is expected if it is looking on the same server as the RES console since the application (ssp) is not deployed there.

However, I cannot seem to configure the RES console to not assume that the ssp is running on the same port.

gold.answer:
First remember to pack all your XOMs (eXecutable Object Model) into the ssp.war following the documentation [http://publib.boulder.ibm.com/infocenter/brjrules/v7r1/topic/com.ibm.websphere.ilog.jrules.doc/Content/Business_Rules/Documentation/_pubskel/JRules/ps_JRules_Global720.html]. 

Then make sure the SSP (ssp.war) is deployed on each server along with a XU connection factory and the appropriate datasource definition. 

 

Then create your own SSP resolver, add it to the teamserver.war and set the teamserver.defaultSSPResolver.class property to this class following this specification [http://publib.boulder.ibm.com/infocenter/brjrules/v7r1/index.jsp?topic=/com.ibm.websphere.ilog.jrules.doc/html/api/html/ilog/rules/teamserver/model/testing/IlrSSPResolver.html]. 

 

By implementing your own method IlrSSPResolver.getSSPURL(String serverName,URL url), you will be able to point to something else than the default provider. 

The default provider uses the url of the Rule Execution Server passed in parameter and replaces the application name with testing. 

A simple implementation can use the server name to return a specific server URL.

answer:
# Pointing Decision Center to a Separate SSP Server

## Understanding the Problem

In your split deployment:

| Server | Port | What's Deployed |
|--------|------|-----------------|
| Mgmt (RES console) | 8000 | `res` application only |
| Runtime | 9000 | SSP EAR, XU, execution units |

When you set the RES endpoint to `http://hostname:8000/res`, Decision Center **hard-codes** the DVS testing call to the same base, i.e. `http://hostname:8000/res/testing/sspService`. That path never exists on the mgmt server, so you get the "host and port are responsive but … cannot be found" error. This is the exact scenario covered by **SWG21615508** (*"Unable to run Test Suites against clustered SSP from Decision Center console"*).

## The Fix – Override the SSP URL System Property

DC/RES reads the SSP endpoint from a JVM-level system property. You set it on the **application server that hosts the Decision Center / RES console** (your port-8000 server), not on the runtime server.

### Step-by-step (WebSphere ND)

1. **Log in** to the WebSphere Admin Console for the **mgmt** server (port 8000).
2. Navigate to:
   ```
   Servers > Server Types > WebSphere application servers
            > [mgmt_server]
   > Java and Process Management
   > Process Definition
   > Custom Properties
   ```
3. **Add (or edit) a custom property:**

   | Field | Value |
   |-------|-------|
   | Name | `com.ibm.rules.res.ssp.url` |
   | Value | `http://hostname:9000/res` |
   | Type | `String` |

   > This tells the RES console that the SSP (including `/testing/sspService`) lives at `http://hostname:9000/res/…` instead of on the local 8000 port.

4. **Restart** the mgmt application server (or at minimum restart the `business-manager` / `res` web application) so the new JVM property is picked up.

Title: IBM Error when executing DVS test from RTS:  "Host and port appear to be responsive but the service "/testing/repositoryService" does not exist." - United States

Text:
 TECHNOTE (TROUBLESHOOTING)

PROBLEM(ABSTRACT)
 When I run a DVS test from RTS, I get the following error: "Host and port appear to be responsive but the service "/testing/repositoryService" does not exist."


RESOLVING THE PROBLEM
 

This might be due to user errors in configuration. For example, you could have set the URL of the Rule Execution Server to be 'http://‹host›:‹port›/testing' instead of 'http://‹host›:‹port›/res" in the RTS configuration. 

. When you add a new server to the RTS configuration ( Websphere ILOG Rule Team Server online help › Configure: Manage your project configuration › Managing servers [http://publib.boulder.ibm.com/infocenter/brdotnet/v7r0m2/index.jsp?topic=/com.ibm.websphere.ilog.brdotnet.doc/Content/Business_Rules/Documentation/_pubskel/Rules_for_DotNET/ps_RFDN_Global716.html]), make sure you specify the URL of the Rule Execution Server (e.g.: http://localhost:8080/res). 

A common mistake is to specify the URL of the SSP server (e.g.: http://localhost:8080/testing), which leads to the error above. 

 

This error could also indicate that the SSP is not correctly deployed or configured. 

Please check that the SSP is correctly deployed and configured. 

Examine the application server logs for error messages which indicate the root of the problem. For example, you could have multiple SSPs deployed and different XOMs

question:
How to configure DC to look on a different App server for the SSP?



I have a single Application server with the RES console installed, and then a separate application server with the XU, the ssp ear, etc. on that one. Each app server is configured separately with respective ports. for example, mgmt server (with the RES console only) has port 8000, and the runtime server (with all of the runtime components) has port 9000.

The problem I am running into is the following:

When I am trying to run a DVS test suite from Decision Center against RES, (my server endpoint in Decision Center is configured as http://hostname:port/res)

I am getting a "the host and port are responsive but the "/testing/sspService" cannot be found. This is expected if it is looking on the same server as the RES console since the application (ssp) is not deployed there.

However, I cannot seem to configure the RES console to not assume that the ssp is running on the same port.

gold.answer:
First remember to pack all your XOMs (eXecutable Object Model) into the ssp.war following the documentation [http://publib.boulder.ibm.com/infocenter/brjrules/v7r1/topic/com.ibm.websphere.ilog.jrules.doc/Content/Business_Rules/Documentation/_pubskel/JRules/ps_JRules_Global720.html]. 

Then make sure the SSP (ssp.war) is deployed on each server along with a XU connection factory and the appropriate datasource definition. 

 

Then create your own SSP resolver, add it to the teamserver.war and set the teamserver.defaultSSPResolver.class property to this class following this specification [http://publib.boulder.ibm.com/infocenter/brjrules/v7r1/index.jsp?topic=/com.ibm.websphere.ilog.jrules.doc/html/api/html/ilog/rules/teamserver/model/testing/IlrSSPResolver.html]. 

 

By implementing your own method IlrSSPResolver.getSSPURL(String serverName,URL url), you will be able to point to something else than the default provider. 

The default provider uses the url of the Rule Execution Server passed in parameter and replaces the application name with testing. 

A simple implementation can use the server name to return a specific server URL.

answer:
# Configuring Decision Center to Reach the SSP on a Separate Runtime Server

## Root Cause

Your Decision Center endpoint is pointing at the **management** server (port 8000, RES console only). When DC executes a DVS test, it calls `/testing/sspService` on that same endpoint. Since the SSP EAR is deployed on the **runtime** server (port 9000), that path doesn't exist on port 8000, producing the error:

> *"The host and port are responsive but `/testing/sspService` cannot be found."*

The source confirms this pattern: the host responds (so the server is up), but the specific SSP context/servlet is absent because it was never deployed there.

## Solutions (pick one)

### Option A – Point the DC endpoint at the runtime server

In **Decision Center → Manage Servers → your server → Edit**, change the endpoint URL from the management port to the runtime port:

```
http://<hostname>:9000/res
```

This is the simplest fix when the management console isn't needed from DC. DC will then reach `/testing/sspService` on the server where the SSP EAR actually lives.

> ⚠️ The source note warns that using the *wrong* server URL (one that doesn't host the SSP) is a common cause of exactly this error, so make sure the URL you enter is the one where `role-execution-server-ear` and the SSP are deployed.

### Option B – Reverse-proxy a single URL in front of both servers

Place an Apache HTTP Server (or WebSphere, Nginx, etc.) on a single public port (say 8443) and use `mod_proxy` / `virtual hosts` to split traffic:

```apache
<VirtualHost *:8443>
  # Management / RES console traffic
  ProxyPass        /res/management  http://mgmt-server:8000/res/management
  ProxyPassReverse /res/management  http://mgmt-server:8000/res/management

  # SSP / runtime traffic (this is what DC hits for DVS tests)
  ProxyPass        /testing/sspService  http://runtime-server:9000/testing/sspService

# Configuring Decision Center to Reach SSP on a Separate Runtime Server

## Understanding the Problem

Your architecture:

```
[Decision Center / DVS]
        │
        ▼
  http://host:8000/res   ← RES Console (MGMT server)
        │
        ├── /res/...     ✅ works (console lives here)
        └── /testing/sspService  ❌ NOT deployed here, it's on :9000
```

The RES Console is hard-wired to assume that the SSP web service (`/testing/sspService`) is co-located on its own context. DVS, when it calls the RES endpoint, gets the SSP URL derived from *that* same host:port.

## Primary Fix – RES `res.properties` (on the MGMT server)

The RES Console reads a properties file (typically `<RES_HOME>/properties/res.properties` or the equivalent location under the console app's config) that defines where the **runtime backend** lives. The key property you need to set is the **runtime / execution server URL**:

```properties
# Point the runtime (where XU + SSP ear are actually deployed) to the
# separate application server.
res.runtime.server.url=http://<runtime-host>:9000
```

Exact property name varies by ODM/DRM version. In some releases it appears as:

| Version family | Property name |
|---|---|
| ODM 8.x / DC 8.x | `res.runtime.service.url` or `res.execution.server.url` |
| ODM 7.5 / DC 7.5 | `res.backend.server.url` |
| Older RES 7.x | set via the RES Console → **Configuration → Backends → (edit backend) → Server URL** |

After editing, **redeploy / restart the RES Console** on the MGMT server so the new URL is picked up.

> **Tip:** If you can't find the property, search the RES properties file (and any included `*.properties`) for the string `8000` or `localhost` – the SSP/runtime URL is often set to the console's own host:port by default, which is exactly the misrouting you're seeing.

## If the Property Doesn't Exist in Your Build – Reverse-Proxy Approach

Some ODM/DC builds do not expose a separate SSP URL knob.
