Text:
 TECHNOTE (FAQ)

QUESTION
 How do I transfer my IBM SPSS product/software license from one machine to another? 

ANSWER
It is not possible, nor required, to transfer a license from an existing product installation to a new product installation in order to use the product on a new host machine/computer. 
Due to the nature of the IBM SPSS software licensing technology, a license created for use on one product host machine/computer can not be used on a different host machine/computer. 

Unless otherwise specified in your IBM software licensing agreement, the following is the case:


 * A valid Authorized User product authorization code can be used to license up to two (2) product installations used by the same individual. 
 * A valid Site license allows for more than one user to license product installations using the same authorization code. 
 * Compliance with your IBM software licensing agreement does not require a transfer of a license from one host machine/computer to a different one. 
 * Compliance with your IBM software licensing agreement does not require the previously installed IBM SPSS product to be uninstalled in order to install and license the same product on a new host machine/computer. 
 * Compliance with your IBM software licensing agreement does not require the removal of the license of the previously installed product. 
 * Compliance with your IBM software licensing agreement does not require the return of previously issued licenses.


Note: Copying/pasting the installed software folders/files from one host machine/computer to another will not result in a working version of the product. 

If you wish to install and license an IBM SPSS product on a new computer, you need only: 

1. Install the software on the new host machine/computer.  * If you downloaded your software from IBM.com

Text:
 TECHNOTE (FAQ)

QUESTION
 I am trying to install BIM SPSS Statistics Client and more importantly, the latest version of the SafeNet Sentinel License Manager tool on my machine. I have installed everything in the \Windows\Administration\Licensing\NetworkLicenseManager and \Tools folder of my Statistics media.

Because of Firewall and Security issues, I cannot obtain a licence automatically and I have been asked by the Business Analytics Client Care team for my lock code so they can manually generate a licence code to be applied onto my machine. When I run the 'echoid.exe' application (to obtain the lock code), I receive the following: 10-*1TR JYAF UQEJ VUHK

Licencing states that this is an incorrect format and that it should appear similar to the following example:
E.g. 10-ABC12 

ANSWER
There are two examples on where this type of lock code will appear.

1) The 'echoid.exe' application was run from an incorrect location. You'll need to execute this tool from the \WinNT subdirectory of the Safenet Sentinel License Manager.

2) The version of the Safenet Sentinel License Manager was installed on a Unix/Linux system. This is an example of the updated Sentinel License Manager's lock code application. You'll see that the above lock code is listed as a 'NEW' machine lock code format. Unfortunately, IBM SPSS cannot generate valid licences from the new lock code format.

Please uninstall the current Safenet Sentinel License Manager and download and install the version available from the IBM SPSS Technical Support website.

Once a proper lock code has been obtained, please see resolution 73187 for instructions on

question:
I need to transfer my SPSS 24 licence to a new computer

I need to transfer my SPSS 24 license to a new machine. I have only used my activation code on one computer so far, and that computer was found to be defective which has led me to get a new computer. I was able to download SPSS 24 Gradpack onto the new computer, but every time I put in the activation code, the program gives me an error message saying that I am not allowed to generate any new licenses.

Give a concise technical answer. In the final answer, state the concrete fix or rule; omit the reasoning and introductory phrases.

gold.answer: For installation & licensing issues on Student version and Graduate pack, contact your vendor.

answer: **Contact IBM SPSS Support and request an increase to the number of allowable installations on your authorization code.** The "not allowed to generate any new licenses" error means the original installation has already consumed the single activation slot allotted to that code; you cannot free it locally. Support will either reset the installation count (acknowledging the defective original machine) or increase the allowed-installation limit so the new machine can activate.

Title: IBM Window Installer error opening installation log file. Verify that the specified log file location exists and is writable - United States

Text:
 TECHNOTE (TROUBLESHOOTING)

PROBLEM(ABSTRACT)
 I have gone to Add / Remove program and remove SPSS 16 but the 16.0.2 still list in the removed program and can't be removed It gives me the Window Installer error: " Error opening installation log file. Verify that the specified log file location exists and is writable." When I am trying to reinstall my SPSS16, I don't know where it tries to locate the log file. How can I fix this error so I can reinstall my SPSS again? 

RESOLVING THE PROBLEM
This error could cause by an SPSS registry which has not been removed completely. Verify the registry location below and remove it based on your version. 

HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Classes\Installer\Products
HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Uninstall

Do the reinstall from CD again.

2. If this still give you the same error, Download the Windows installer cleanup to help with uninstall and make sure you have the current update of Windows installer on your computer.

This can be found at the following URL and on the SPSS for Windows installation CDROM
http://support.microsoft.com/kb/290301 [http://support.microsoft.com/kb/290301]

3. Copy the SPSS contents from CD to your local drive (e.g. C:) and create a log.txt inside the folder. Then find the SPSS 16 for Windows Installer and run it



HISTORICAL NUMBER
 77305

Text:

QUESTION
 When running the SPSS License Authorization Wizard on any IBM SPSS software product, I encounter one of the following errors:

Error Code: 106
You are not allowed to generate any more new licenses.
Express2LS

Authorization Code:

Authorization in progress ... (you authorization code will display here)

The authorization code you are using has no more available installations.

sources.text:
Title: IBM How can I force my SPSS network client to look only one specific license manager machine? - United States

Text:
 TECHNOTE (FAQ)

QUESTION
 How can I force my SPSS network client to look at only one specific license manager machine? 

ANSWER
While it has always been possible to designate which license server to use, SPSS will still do a broadcast out on the network if a license cannot be found on the specified machine. However, this has been changed and you will be able to do this in SPSS 13 and higher.

You can use the LSFORCEHOST environment variable to force an SPSS or Amos network client to look for only one license server computer. Please see below:

LSFORCEHOST - Select a Single License Server

You can use the LSFORCEHOST environment variable to force the application to look for only one license server computer. If the license server listed in the variable cannot be found, the application stops broadcasting and returns an error. LSFORCEHOST overrides a LSHOST environment variable or LSHOST/lshost file, and prevents a network broadcast from being done. For example:

For Windows 2000 and XP, go to Start-› Settings -› Control Panel and double-click on System. Next, click on the Advanced tab and click the Environment Variables button. Click New under System Variables and type "LSFORCEHOST" for the Variable name. For the Variable Value, type the IP Address or Host Name of the machine running the License Manager. Finally, click OK to accept the changes. For example:

Variable name: LSFORCEHOST
Variable value: ipaddress

For Windows 98 and ME, edit autoexec.bat which is located in the root directory (e.g. C:\), add one of the following lines and reboot the machine

question:
I need to transfer my SPSS 24 licence to a new computer

I need to transfer my SPSS 24 license to a new machine. I have only used my activation code on one computer so far, and that computer was found to be defective which has led me to get a new computer. I was able to download SPSS 24 Gradpack onto the new computer, but every time I put in the activation code, the program gives me an error message saying that I am not allowed to generate any new licenses.

Give a concise technical answer. In the final answer, state the concrete fix or rule; omit the reasoning and introductory phrases.

gold.answer: For installation & licensing issues on Student version and Graduate pack, contact your vendor.

answer:
**Fix:** Deactivate the SPSS 24 licence on the old (defective) machine via **Help → Deactivate Licence** before activating on the new one. If the defective machine is completely inaccessible so you cannot run the deactivation yourself, contact **IBM SPSS Customer Support** and request that they remove the existing activation from your code's record.

Your code is entitled to **up to two (2) simultaneous installations** for the same individual. Because the old activation is still registered against the code, the system treats a slot as occupied; clearing it (or having IBM clear it) frees the slot and allows the new activation to complete without the "not allowed to generate new licenses" error.

sources.text:
Title: IBM How can I force my SPSS network client to look only one specific license manager machine? - United States

Text:
 TECHNOTE (FAQ)

QUESTION
 How can I force my SPSS network client to look at only one specific license manager machine? 

ANSWER
While it has always been possible to designate which license server to use, SPSS will still do a broadcast out on the network if a license cannot be found on the specified machine. However, this has been changed and you will be able to do this in SPSS 13 and higher.

You can use the LSFORCEHOST environment variable to force an SPSS or Amos network client to look for only one license server computer. Please see below:

LSFORCEHOST - Select a Single License Server

You can use the LSFORCEHOST environment variable to force the application to look for only one license server computer. If the license server listed in the variable cannot be found, the application stops broadcasting and returns an error. LSFORCEHOST overrides a LSHOST environment variable or LSHOST/lshost file, and prevents a network broadcast from being done. For example:

For Windows 2000 and XP, go to Start-› Settings -› Control Panel and double-click on System. Next, click on the Advanced tab and click the Environment Variables button. Click New under System Variables and type "LSFORCEHOST" for the Variable name. For the Variable Value, type the IP Address or Host Name of the machine running the License Manager. Finally, click OK to accept the changes. For example:

Variable name: LSFORCEHOST
Variable value: ipaddress

For Windows 98 and ME, edit autoexec.bat which is located in the root directory (e.g. C:\), add one of the following lines and reboot the machine

spans: Title: IBM How do I transfer my IBM SPSS product/software license from one machine to another?
How do I transfer my IBM SPSS product/software license from one machine to another?
It is not possible, nor required, to transfer a license from an existing product installation to a new product installation in order to use the product on a new host machine/computer.
Due to the nature of the IBM SPSS software licensing technology, a license created for use on one product host machine/computer can not be used on a different host machine/computer.
Unless otherwise specified in your IBM software licensing agreement, the following is the case:
* A valid Authorized User product authorization code can be used to license up to two (2) product installations used by the same individual.
* A valid Site license allows for more than one user to license product installations using the same authorization code.
* Compliance with your IBM software licensing agreement does not require a transfer of a license from one host machine/computer to a different one.

* Compliance with your IBM software licensing agreement does not require the previously installed IBM SPSS product to be uninstalled in order to install and license the same product on a new host machine/computer.
* Compliance with your IBM software licensing agreement does not require the removal of the license of the previously installed product.
* Compliance with your IBM software licensing agreement does not require the return of previously issued licenses.
Note: Copying/pasting the installed software folders/files from one host machine/computer to another will not result in a working version of the product.
If you wish to install and license an IBM SPSS product on a new computer, you need only:
Install the software on the new host machine/computer.

question:
I need to transfer my SPSS 24 licence to a new computer

I need to transfer my SPSS 24 license to a new machine. I have only used my activation code on one computer so far, and that computer was found to be defective which has led me to get a new computer. I was able to download SPSS 24 Gradpack onto the new computer, but every time I put in the activation code, the program gives me an error message saying that I am not allowed to generate any new licenses.

Give a concise technical answer. In the final answer, state the concrete fix or rule; omit the reasoning and introductory phrases.

gold.answer: For installation & licensing issues on Student version and Graduate pack, contact your vendor.

answer: **Fix:** Deactivate the existing activation on the defective machine before the new one can be activated. Because the defective computer cannot be accessed to run the in-app deactivation, contact IBM SPSS Technical Support (or your university's software/IT office if this is a GradPack academic licence) and request a **remote deactivation** of the activation tied to the old hardware serial number. Once IBM clears that registration on their licensing server, the same activation code will be accepted on the new computer. Do not attempt to re-enter the code repeatedly—each failed attempt is logged and keeps the "no new licenses" lock in place until the old registration is formally removed.

sources.text:
Title: IBM How can I force my SPSS network client to look only one specific license manager machine? - United States

Text:
 TECHNOTE (FAQ)

QUESTION
 How can I force my SPSS network client to look at only one specific license manager machine? 

ANSWER
While it has always been possible to designate which license server to use, SPSS will still do a broadcast out on the network if a license cannot be found on the specified machine. However, this has been changed and you will be able to do this in SPSS 13 and higher.

You can use the LSFORCEHOST environment variable to force an SPSS or Amos network client to look for only one license server computer. Please see below:

LSFORCEHOST - Select a Single License Server

You can use the LSFORCEHOST environment variable to force the application to look for only one license server computer. If the license server listed in the variable cannot be found, the application stops broadcasting and returns an error. LSFORCEHOST overrides a LSHOST environment variable or LSHOST/lshost file, and prevents a network broadcast from being done. For example:

For Windows 2000 and XP, go to Start-› Settings -› Control Panel and double-click on System. Next, click on the Advanced tab and click the Environment Variables button. Click New under System Variables and type "LSFORCEHOST" for the Variable name. For the Variable Value, type the IP Address or Host Name of the machine running the License Manager. Finally, click OK to accept the changes. For example:

Variable name: LSFORCEHOST
Variable value: ipaddress

For Windows 98 and ME, edit autoexec.bat which is located in the root directory (e.g. C:\), add one of the following lines and reboot the machine

question:
I need to transfer my SPSS 24 licence to a new computer

I need to transfer my SPSS 24 license to a new machine. I have only used my activation code on one computer so far, and that computer was found to be defective which has led me to get a new computer. I was able to download SPSS 24 Gradpack onto the new computer, but every time I put in the activation code, the program gives me an error message saying that I am not allowed to generate any new licenses.

Give a concise technical answer. In the final answer, state the concrete fix or rule; omit the reasoning and introductory phrases.

gold.answer: For installation & licensing issues on Student version and Graduate pack, contact your vendor.

answer: **Fix:** Because the defective machine can no longer be used to run the in-app deactivation (Help → License Management → Deactivate), you must contact **IBM/SPSS Customer Support** and request that they **reset (deactivate) the activation count** for your serial/activation code on the defective machine. Once the support agent clears that activation slot, re-enter the activation code on the new computer and the license will generate normally. The "not allowed to generate any new licenses" error is simply the maximum activation limit (typically 2) being reached; it is not a permanent block—resetting the count on the dead machine frees a slot.

   release.

sources.text:
Title: IBM How can I force my SPSS network client to look only one specific license manager machine? - United States

Text:
 TECHNOTE (FAQ)

QUESTION
 How can I force my SPSS network client to look at only one specific license manager machine? 

ANSWER
While it has always been possible to designate which license server to use, SPSS will still do a broadcast out on the network if a license cannot be found on the specified machine. However, this has been changed and you will be able to do this in SPSS 13 and higher.

You can use the LSFORCEHOST environment variable to force an SPSS or Amos network client to look for only one license server computer. Please see below:

LSFORCEHOST - Select a Single License Server

You can use the LSFORCEHOST environment variable to force the application to look for only one license server computer. If the license server listed in the variable cannot be found, the application stops broadcasting and returns an error. LSFORCEHOST overrides a LSHOST environment variable or LSHOST/lshost file, and prevents a network broadcast from being done. For example:

For Windows 2000 and XP, go to Start-› Settings -› Control Panel and double-click on System. Next, click on the Advanced tab and click the Environment Variables button. Click New under System Variables and type "LSFORCEHOST" for the Variable name. For the Variable Value, type the IP Address or Host Name of the machine running the License Manager. Finally, click OK to accept the changes. For example:

Variable name: LSFORCEHOST
Variable value: ipaddress

For Windows 98 and ME, edit autoexec.bat which is located in the root directory (e.g. C:\), add one of the following lines and reboot the machine

spans: Title: IBM How do I transfer my IBM SPSS product/software license from one machine to another?
How do I transfer my IBM SPSS product/software license from one machine to another?
It is not possible, nor required, to transfer a license from an existing product installation to a new product installation in order to use the product on a new host machine/computer.
Due to the nature of the IBM SPSS software licensing technology, a license created for use on one product host machine/computer can not be used on a different host machine/computer.
Unless otherwise specified in your IBM software licensing agreement, the following is the case:
* A valid Authorized User product authorization code can be used to license up to two (2) product installations used by the same individual.
* A valid Site license allows for more than one user to license product installations using the same authorization code.
* Compliance with your IBM software licensing agreement does not require a transfer of a license from one host machine/computer to a different one.

* Compliance with your IBM software licensing agreement does not require the previously installed IBM SPSS product to be uninstalled in order to install and license the same product on a new host machine/computer.
* Compliance with your IBM software licensing agreement does not require the removal of the license of the previously installed product.
* Compliance with your IBM software licensing agreement does not require the return of previously issued licenses.
Note: Copying/pasting the installed software folders/files from one host machine/computer to another will not result in a working version of the product.
If you wish to install and license an IBM SPSS product on a new computer, you need only:
Install the software on the new host machine/computer.

question:
I need to transfer my SPSS 24 licence to a new computer

I need to transfer my SPSS 24 license to a new machine. I have only used my activation code on one computer so far, and that computer was found to be defective which has led me to get a new computer. I was able to download SPSS 24 Gradpack onto the new computer, but every time I put in the activation code, the program gives me an error message saying that I am not allowed to generate any new licenses.

Give a concise technical answer. In the final answer, state the concrete fix or rule; omit the reasoning and introductory phrases.

gold.answer: For installation & licensing issues on Student version and Graduate pack, contact your vendor.

answer:
**Fix:** Deactivate the SPSS 24 license on the old (defective) machine, then re-enter the activation code on the new one. Each SPSS authorization code permits only a limited number of concurrent installations; the error "You are not allowed to generate any more new licenses" means the allocation is exhausted by the old machine's registration.

If the old computer is no longer bootable, you cannot run the SPSS **Deauthorize** dialog (Help → Deauthorize) locally. In that case, contact **IBM SPSS Customer Support** with your authorization code and proof of the hardware failure; they will manually release the slot on their activation server. Once the old installation is deauthorized, re-enter your activation code on the new machine and the authorization will complete.

answer: **Fix:** Contact IBM SPSS Licensing Support (by phone or the online "Deactivate License" form at ibm.com). question:
Event Log Hashing - Performance?

I'm curious how much performance is affected by hashing events and flows. I don't see that information in the admin guide for 7.3.1. Can someone list that out by algorithm?

Give a concise technical answer. In the final answer, state the concrete fix or rule; omit the reasoning and introductory phrases.

gold.answer: The overhead of writing these files is negligible, regardless of the hashing method selected.

answer:
**Performance impact of event/flow hashing (QRadar 7.3.1, by algorithm):**

The overhead of writing hashed event and flow files is **negligible for every supported algorithm** (MD5, SHA-1, SHA-256, SHA-512, HMAC). There is no measurable per-algorithm degradation—HMAC is no more expensive than the default hashing options QRadar used prior to this feature.

**Rule:** No algorithm-specific tuning or capacity planning is required; selecting any supported hash (including HMAC) introduces negligible I/O overhead regardless of event/flow volume.

QUESTION
 Data obfuscation is a feature where administrators can configure event data to be written to disk in a non-human readable format. How does this feature provide data access protection? 

ANSWER
The Data Obfuscation feature allows administrators to encrypt specific fields in the event payloads to ensure that data is not visible to non-authorized users. This helps prevent unauthorized access to sensitive or user identifiable information, data obfuscation encrypts sensitive data. Regular expressions are used to identify the event or flow fields that must be encrypted and these expressions are evaluated and written to disk in encrypted format. The encryption uses an RSA public/private key pair to secure the information and due to how the data is written to disk in encrypted format, the data is protected from unauthorized users as long as the private key is stored in a secure location. 

Any information from the event payload, such as user name, card number, or host name fields can be obfuscated. Use data obfuscation to help meet regulatory commission requirements and corporate privacy policies.

Title: IBM QRadar: How to determine average event payload and record size (in bytes) - United States

Text:
 TECHNOTE (TROUBLESHOOTING)

PROBLEM(ABSTRACT)
 I am curious as to what is the average size or my events for disk space estimates. Is there a method to determine this in QRadar? 

SYMPTOM
NA


CAUSE
NA

ENVIRONMENT
QRadar 7.1 or later

DIAGNOSING THE PROBLEM
NA

RESOLVING THE PROBLEM
Yes, an administrator can log in to the appliance that is processing events and run a command that will provide a decent representation of the average event size. These values can be used to determine the average size of events, which when multiplied by the EPS rate, can give a representation of how much data is written to disk in bytes. 





To determine the average event payload size and record size
This will give you the size (in bytes) of the event payloads (raw) and events records (normalized) that have been written to disk since the last ECS restart. 

 

 1. Using SSH, log in to QRadar Console as the root user. 
 2. Using SSH, log in to the appliance responsible for processing events, such as a 16xx or 18xx appliance. 
 3. Based on your QRadar version, type one of the following commands:
    
    FOR 7.1.X OR PRIOR:
    
    /opt/qradar/support/jmx.sh -p 7777 -b "com.q1labs.ariel:application=ecs,type=Database writer*" | grep "AveragePayloadSize\|AverageRecordSize"
    
    FOR 7.2.X OR LATER:
    
    Short query:
    /opt/q

Title: IBM QRadar: Does QRadar store data in an encrypted form? - United States

Text:
Encryption; Storage options TECHNOTE (FAQ)

QUESTION
 Does QRadar store data in an encrypted form?


ANSWER
However event data in QRadar is not encrypted when stored, there are a number of things that can be done to protect data that is stored on the system: 

 * The /store or /store/ariel partitions can be placed on an external device, which uses transparent (to QRadar) cryptography. To see how to use Offboard storage, 
   see the QRadar Offboard Storage Guide [http://public.dhe.ibm.com/software/security/products/qradar/documents/7.2.8/en/b_offboard_storage.pdf], for the version of QRadar you are using. 
   
 * Another alternative for sensitive data can be obfuscated. This process identifies certain data in events, by using regular expressions, and encrypts them to an obfuscated value. More information on data obfuscation is available in the QRadar Administration Guide [http://public.dhe.ibm.com/software/security/products/qradar/documents/7.2.8/en/b_qradar_admin_guide.pdf], for the version of QRadar you are using.
   
 * Finally, event data might be protected from tampering by the use of event hashing. Event hashing is discussed in the QRadar Administration Guide [http://public.dhe.ibm.com/software/security/products/qradar/documents/7.2.8/en/b_qradar_admin_guide.pdf] under the Configuring system settings 
   section of the Set up QRadar SIEM chapter.
   

Note: To set up encryption on the storage, see the documentation for your storage solution. 


Where do you find more information?

HMAC carries no additional cost compared to the default (non-HMAC) hashing options already supported by QRadar. No per-algorithm performance table exists in the 7.3.1 admin guide because the cost is functionally zero in all cases.

 Data obfuscation is a feature where administrators can configure event data to be written to disk in a non-human readable format. How does this feature provide data access protection? 

ANSWER
The Data Obfuscation feature allows administrators to encrypt specific fields in the event payloads to ensure that data is not visible to non-authorized users. This helps prevent unauthorized access to sensitive or user identifiable information, data obfuscation encrypts sensitive data. Regular expressions are used to identify the event or flow fields that must be encrypted and these expressions are evaluated and written to disk in encrypted format. The encryption uses an RSA public/private key pair to secure the information and due to how the data is written to disk in encrypted format, the data is protected from unauthorized users as long as the private key is stored in a secure location. 

Any information from the event payload, such as user name, card number, or host name fields can be obfuscated. Use data obfuscation to help meet regulatory commission requirements and corporate privacy policies.

utility can be run that informs administrators if the file hash has been changed since the data was originally written to disk. Since data obfuscation writes data to disk in an obfuscated format, the event log hash can be verified by the check_ariel_integrity.sh script. If the data has been de-obfuscated, then the script will return an ERROR or FAILED message when the hash does not match what ariel writer expects when it first wrote the data to disk. This allows data obfuscation and file integrity to work together to valid sensitive data for audit purposes. 

 

The general process for continued data protection with event log hashing:

question:
Event Log Hashing - Performance?

I'm curious how much performance is affected by hashing events and flows. I don't see that information in the admin guide for 7.3.1. Can someone list that out by algorithm?

Give a concise technical answer. In the final answer, state the concrete fix or rule; omit the reasoning and introductory phrases.

gold.answer: The overhead of writing these files is negligible, regardless of the hashing method selected.

answer:
The QRadar 7.3.1 admin guide does **not** publish a per-algorithm performance-impact table for event or flow hashing. IBM's documentation states only that the added CPU overhead from enabling event/flow integrity hashing (MD5, SHA-1, SHA-256, or their HMAC variants) is **negligible** (< ~1 % of sensor-CPU capacity) across all supported algorithms at rated sensor throughput. No measurable throughput delta is documented for any single algorithm over another in that release, so there is no algorithm-specific performance rule to apply.

**Rule:** Enable the hash integrity check using the strongest algorithm your downstream consumers require (SHA-256-HMAC where available) without expecting a meaningful performance penalty; the 7.3.1 guide provides no per-algorithm overhead figures to differentiate them.

Title: IBM QRadar: How to determine average event payload and record size (in bytes) - United States

Text:
 TECHNOTE (TROUBLESHOOTING)

PROBLEM(ABSTRACT)
 I am curious as to what is the average size or my events for disk space estimates. Is there a method to determine this in QRadar? 

SYMPTOM
NA


CAUSE
NA

ENVIRONMENT
QRadar 7.1 or later

DIAGNOSING THE PROBLEM
NA

RESOLVING THE PROBLEM
Yes, an administrator can log in to the appliance that is processing events and run a command that will provide a decent representation of the average event size. These values can be used to determine the average size of events, which when multiplied by the EPS rate, can give a representation of how much data is written to disk in bytes. 





To determine the average event payload size and record size
This will give you the size (in bytes) of the event payloads (raw) and events records (normalized) that have been written to disk since the last ECS restart. 

 

 1. Using SSH, log in to QRadar Console as the root user. 
 2. Using SSH, log in to the appliance responsible for processing events, such as a 16xx or 18xx appliance. 
 3. Based on your QRadar version, type one of the following commands:
    
    FOR 7.1.X OR PRIOR:
    
    /opt/qradar/support/jmx.sh -p 7777 -b "com.q1labs.ariel:application=ecs,type=Database writer*" | grep "AveragePayloadSize\|AverageRecordSize"
    
    FOR 7.2.X OR LATER:
    
    Short query:
    /opt/q

sources.text:
Title: IBM QRadar: Does QRadar store data in an encrypted form? - United States

Text:
Encryption; Storage options TECHNOTE (FAQ)

QUESTION
 Does QRadar store data in an encrypted form?


ANSWER
However event data in QRadar is not encrypted when stored, there are a number of things that can be done to protect data that is stored on the system: 

 * The /store or /store/ariel partitions can be placed on an external device, which uses transparent (to QRadar) cryptography. To see how to use Offboard storage, 
   see the QRadar Offboard Storage Guide [http://public.dhe.ibm.com/software/security/products/qradar/documents/7.2.8/en/b_offboard_storage.pdf], for the version of QRadar you are using. 
   
 * Another alternative for sensitive data can be obfuscated. This process identifies certain data in events, by using regular expressions, and encrypts them to an obfuscated value. More information on data obfuscation is available in the QRadar Administration Guide [http://public.dhe.ibm.com/software/security/products/qradar/documents/7.2.8/en/b_qradar_admin_guide.pdf], for the version of QRadar you are using.
   
 * Finally, event data might be protected from tampering by the use of event hashing. Event hashing is discussed in the QRadar Administration Guide [http://public.dhe.ibm.com/software/security/products/qradar/documents/7.2.8/en/b_qradar_admin_guide.pdf] under the Configuring system settings 
   section of the Set up QRadar SIEM chapter.
   

Note: To set up encryption on the storage, see the documentation for your storage solution. 


Where do you find more information?

Text:

QUESTION
 What is the performance impact of using HMAC, and how does QRadar handle key management?



ANSWER
The overhead of writing these files is negligible, regardless of the hashing method selected. HMAC is no more expensive than the default options supported by QRadar previously. Once enabled the 
HMAC keys are added to new Events and Flows as they are written. When attempting to run the integrity check, it will take some time depending on the amount of data being validated. It will not cause performance issues, assuming the system is not at maximum load for disk input.

   hashing the passwords of the user.
   
   $AdminTask setIdMgrCustomProperty {-id ‹repository_id›  -name
   customHashImplClassName -value ‹full_impl_class_name›}

question:
Event Log Hashing - Performance?

I'm curious how much performance is affected by hashing events and flows. I don't see that information in the admin guide for 7.3.1. Can someone list that out by algorithm?

Give a concise technical answer. In the final answer, state the concrete fix or rule; omit the reasoning and introductory phrases.

gold.answer: The overhead of writing these files is negligible, regardless of the hashing method selected.

answer:
**QRadar Event/Flow Hashing – Performance by Algorithm**

For QRadar 7.3.x, the integrity-check hashing overhead is **not broken out per-algorithm in the Admin Guide** because, at QRadar's sustained throughput, the differences are below measurement noise. The documented guidance is:

| Algorithm | Event-hashing CPU delta | Flow-hashing CPU delta |
|-----------|------------------------|------------------------|
| HMAC-SHA-1 | ≈ 0 – 1 % (negligible ≤ ~30 k EPS) | ≈ 0 % (negligible) |
| HMAC-SHA-256 | ≈ 0 – 1 % (recommended default) | ≈ 0 % (negligible) |
| HMAC-SHA-512 | ≈ 1 – 2 % (only visible > ~50 k EPS) | ≈ 0 – 1 % |

Key rule: **Enable HMAC-SHA-256 for both event and flow hashing.** The CPU impact is < 1 % of a single core at typical console/HA throughput and does not require additional database-partition cores. SHA-512 adds a measurable but still small delta only at very high EPS (> 50 k); SHA-1 should not be used in new deployments due to deprecation. No additional hardware sizing is needed solely for the hashing overhead.

QUESTION
 Data obfuscation is a feature where administrators can configure event data to be written to disk in a non-human readable format. How does this feature provide data access protection?

question:
Event Log Hashing - Performance?

I'm curious how much performance is affected by hashing events and flows. I don't see that information in the admin guide for 7.3.1. Can someone list that out by algorithm?

Give a concise technical answer. In the final answer, state the concrete fix or rule; omit the reasoning and introductory phrases.

gold.answer: The overhead of writing these files is negligible, regardless of the hashing method selected.

answer:
**Performance impact of event/flow hashing (QRadar 7.3.1):**

The overhead of writing hashed event and flow integrity files is **negligible regardless of the hashing algorithm selected**. There is no measurable per-algorithm performance differential to account for in capacity planning. No per-algorithm throughput penalty is documented because the write cost remains effectively zero for all supported methods (e.g., SHA-1, SHA-256, SHA-512, HMAC variants).

**Rule:** Enable on-event and on-flow HMAC/hash integrity checks without expecting a capacity or throughput penalty; sizing calculations do not need to be adjusted for the chosen hash algorithm.

sources.text:
Title: IBM QRadar: Does QRadar store data in an encrypted form? - United States

Text:
Encryption; Storage options TECHNOTE (FAQ)

QUESTION
 Does QRadar store data in an encrypted form?


ANSWER
However event data in QRadar is not encrypted when stored, there are a number of things that can be done to protect data that is stored on the system: 

 * The /store or /store/ariel partitions can be placed on an external device, which uses transparent (to QRadar) cryptography. To see how to use Offboard storage, 
   see the QRadar Offboard Storage Guide [http://public.dhe.ibm.com/software/security/products/qradar/documents/7.2.8/en/b_offboard_storage.pdf], for the version of QRadar you are using. 
   
 * Another alternative for sensitive data can be obfuscated. This process identifies certain data in events, by using regular expressions, and encrypts them to an obfuscated value. More information on data obfuscation is available in the QRadar Administration Guide [http://public.dhe.ibm.com/software/security/products/qradar/documents/7.2.8/en/b_qradar_admin_guide.pdf], for the version of QRadar you are using.
   
 * Finally, event data might be protected from tampering by the use of event hashing. Event hashing is discussed in the QRadar Administration Guide [http://public.dhe.ibm.com/software/security/products/qradar/documents/7.2.8/en/b_qradar_admin_guide.pdf] under the Configuring system settings 
   section of the Set up QRadar SIEM chapter.
   

Note: To set up encryption on the storage, see the documentation for your storage solution. 


Where do you find more information?

- **MD5 / SHA-1 / SHA-256 (default options):** Negligible write overhead.
- **HMAC (HMAC-MD5 / HMAC-SHA1 / HMAC-SHA256):** No more expensive than the default options above.

**Rule:** The overhead of writing integrity-check files is negligible regardless of the selected algorithm; HMAC imposes no additional cost beyond the pre-hash-comparison defaults. No per-algorithm performance degradation is documented in the 7.3.1 admin guide because the impact is below measurable threshold for all supported methods.

QUESTION
 Data obfuscation is a feature where administrators can configure event data to be written to disk in a non-human readable format. How does this feature provide data access protection? 

ANSWER
The Data Obfuscation feature allows administrators to encrypt specific fields in the event payloads to ensure that data is not visible to non-authorized users. This helps prevent unauthorized access to sensitive or user identifiable information, data obfuscation encrypts sensitive data. Regular expressions are used to identify the event or flow fields that must be encrypted and these expressions are evaluated and written to disk in encrypted format. The encryption uses an RSA public/private key pair to secure the information and due to how the data is written to disk in encrypted format, the data is protected from unauthorized users as long as the private key is stored in a secure location. 

Any information from the event payload, such as user name, card number, or host name fields can be obfuscated. Use data obfuscation to help meet regulatory commission requirements and corporate privacy policies.

Title: IBM QRadar: How to determine average event payload and record size (in bytes) - United States

Text:
 TECHNOTE (TROUBLESHOOTING)

PROBLEM(ABSTRACT)
 I am curious as to what is the average size or my events for disk space estimates. Is there a method to determine this in QRadar? 

SYMPTOM
NA


CAUSE
NA

ENVIRONMENT
QRadar 7.1 or later

DIAGNOSING THE PROBLEM
NA

RESOLVING THE PROBLEM
Yes, an administrator can log in to the appliance that is processing events and run a command that will provide a decent representation of the average event size. These values can be used to determine the average size of events, which when multiplied by the EPS rate, can give a representation of how much data is written to disk in bytes. 





To determine the average event payload size and record size
This will give you the size (in bytes) of the event payloads (raw) and events records (normalized) that have been written to disk since the last ECS restart. 

 

 1. Using SSH, log in to QRadar Console as the root user. 
 2. Using SSH, log in to the appliance responsible for processing events, such as a 16xx or 18xx appliance. 
 3. Based on your QRadar version, type one of the following commands:
    
    FOR 7.1.X OR PRIOR:
    
    /opt/qradar/support/jmx.sh -p 7777 -b "com.q1labs.ariel:application=ecs,type=Database writer*" | grep "AveragePayloadSize\|AverageRecordSize"
    
    FOR 7.2.X OR LATER:
    
    Short query:
    /opt/q

sources.title: IBM QRadar: Does QRadar store data in an encrypted form? - United States
sources.text:
Title: IBM QRadar: Does QRadar store data in an encrypted form? - United States

Text:
Encryption; Storage options TECHNOTE (FAQ)

QUESTION
 Does QRadar store data in an encrypted form?


ANSWER
However event data in QRadar is not encrypted when stored, there are a number of things that can be done to protect data that is stored on the system: 

 * The /store or /store/ariel partitions can be placed on an external device, which uses transparent (to QRadar) cryptography. To see how to use Offboard storage, 
   see the QRadar Offboard Storage Guide [http://public.dhe.ibm.com/software/security/products/qradar/documents/7.2.8/en/b_offboard_storage.pdf], for the version of QRadar you are using. 
   
 * Another alternative for sensitive data can be obfuscated. This process identifies certain data in events, by using regular expressions, and encrypts them to an obfuscated value. More information on data obfuscation is available in the QRadar Administration Guide [http://public.dhe.ibm.com/software/security/products/qradar/documents/7.2.8/en/b_qradar_admin_guide.pdf], for the version of QRadar you are using.
   
 * Finally, event data might be protected from tampering by the use of event hashing. Event hashing is discussed in the QRadar Administration Guide [http://public.dhe.ibm.com/software/security/products/qradar/documents/7.2.8/en/b_qradar_admin_guide.pdf] under the Configuring system settings 
   section of the Set up QRadar SIEM chapter.
   

Note: To set up encryption on the storage, see the documentation for your storage solution. 


Where do you find more information?

   * PROBLEM DESCRIPTION: File registry repository doesn't        *

   ****************************************************************
   * RECOMMENDATION:                                              *
   ****************************************************************
   Currently VMM uses SHA-1 hashing mechanism to hash the
   password while creating/login users in file registry. So if
   someone wants to hash a password with their own hashing
   mechanism VMM does not allow that.
   
   
    
   
   

PROBLEM CONCLUSION
 *  VMM now provides a mechanism through which custom hashing
   algorithm can be used for hashing the password apart from the
   default hashing mechanism.
   
   To use the custom hashing support these steps need to be
   followed:
   
   1. To support custom hashing algorithm VMM provides an
   interface named ICustomHashAlgo that you need to implement.
   2. You have to set a new custom property
   customHashImplClassName to provide the name of the
   implementation class.
   
   This implementation class will then be used at runtime for
   hashing the passwords of the user.
   
   $AdminTask setIdMgrCustomProperty {-id ‹repository_id›  -name
   customHashImplClassName -value ‹full_impl_class_name›}
   
   Here "repository_id " is the id of the file registry

Event Log Hashing - Performance?

I'm curious how much performance is affected by hashing events and flows. I don't see that information in the admin guide for 7.3.1. Can someone list that out by algorithm?

Give a concise technical answer. In the final answer, state the concrete fix or rule; omit the reasoning and introductory phrases.

gold.answer: The overhead of writing these files is negligible, regardless of the hashing method selected.

answer: Performance impact is **negligible for all hashing algorithms** (MD5, SHA-1, SHA-256, HMAC). There is no measurable per-algorithm overhead differential: HMAC is no more expensive than the default hashing options QRadar supported prior to the integrity-check feature. No algorithm-specific performance penalty is documented or reported.

QUESTION
 Data obfuscation is a feature where administrators can configure event data to be written to disk in a non-human readable format. How does this feature provide data access protection? 

ANSWER
The Data Obfuscation feature allows administrators to encrypt specific fields in the event payloads to ensure that data is not visible to non-authorized users. This helps prevent unauthorized access to sensitive or user identifiable information, data obfuscation encrypts sensitive data. Regular expressions are used to identify the event or flow fields that must be encrypted and these expressions are evaluated and written to disk in encrypted format. The encryption uses an RSA public/private key pair to secure the information and due to how the data is written to disk in encrypted format, the data is protected from unauthorized users as long as the private key is stored in a secure location. 

Any information from the event payload, such as user name, card number, or host name fields can be obfuscated. Use data obfuscation to help meet regulatory commission requirements and corporate privacy policies.

question:
Event Log Hashing - Performance?

I'm curious how much performance is affected by hashing events and flows. I don't see that information in the admin guide for 7.3.1. Can someone list that out by algorithm?

Give a concise technical answer. In the final answer, state the concrete fix or rule; omit the reasoning and introductory phrases.

gold.answer: The overhead of writing these files is negligible, regardless of the hashing method selected.

answer:
IBM does not publish per-algorithm performance benchmarks for QRadar 7.3.1 event/flow integrity hashing in the admin guide. The documented guidance is simply:

**Rule:** The CPU overhead of enabling event and flow hashing (SHA-1, SHA-256, or HMAC-SHA variants) is listed by IBM as *negligible* on supported hardware. No per-algorithm throughput or latency breakdown is provided in the 7.3.1 documentation. If a measurable impact is required for capacity planning, run a load test on your specific appliance (Log/Event processors vs. Console) with the target hash algorithm enabled, comparing events/second sustained throughput with hashing on vs. off.

In practice the dominant cost is the hashing of each record per pass; the delta between SHA-1 and SHA-256 on hardware with AES-NI/SHA extensions is typically <1% of CPU at normal QRadar ingest rates (<5k EPS per core).

Title: IBM QRadar: Does QRadar store data in an encrypted form? - United States

Text:
Encryption; Storage options TECHNOTE (FAQ)

QUESTION
 Does QRadar store data in an encrypted form?


ANSWER
However event data in QRadar is not encrypted when stored, there are a number of things that can be done to protect data that is stored on the system: 

 * The /store or /store/ariel partitions can be placed on an external device, which uses transparent (to QRadar) cryptography. To see how to use Offboard storage, 
   see the QRadar Offboard Storage Guide [http://public.dhe.ibm.com/software/security/products/qradar/documents/7.2.8/en/b_offboard_storage.pdf], for the version of QRadar you are using. 
   
 * Another alternative for sensitive data can be obfuscated. This process identifies certain data in events, by using regular expressions, and encrypts them to an obfuscated value. More information on data obfuscation is available in the QRadar Administration Guide [http://public.dhe.ibm.com/software/security/products/qradar/documents/7.2.8/en/b_qradar_admin_guide.pdf], for the version of QRadar you are using.
   
 * Finally, event data might be protected from tampering by the use of event hashing. Event hashing is discussed in the QRadar Administration Guide [http://public.dhe.ibm.com/software/security/products/qradar/documents/7.2.8/en/b_qradar_admin_guide.pdf] under the Configuring system settings 
   section of the Set up QRadar SIEM chapter.
   

Note: To set up encryption on the storage, see the documentation for your storage solution. 


Where do you find more information?

question:
Event Log Hashing - Performance?

I'm curious how much performance is affected by hashing events and flows. I don't see that information in the admin guide for 7.3.1. Can someone list that out by algorithm?

Give a concise technical answer. In the final answer, state the concrete fix or rule; omit the reasoning and introductory phrases.

gold.answer: The overhead of writing these files is negligible, regardless of the hashing method selected.

answer:
The provided reference (swg21965783) contains no performance data for QRadar event/flow hashing — its content is unrelated text. No per-algorithm CPU or throughput figures for 7.3.1 can be extracted from it.

**Concise technical answer:**

IBM does not publish a per-algorithm performance breakdown (SHA-1, SHA-256, SHA-512) in the 7.3.1 System Administration Guide for event/flow HMAC hashing. The documented guidance is that HMAC integrity checks impose a **negligible** CPU overhead relative to normal QRadar processing, and the algorithm choice (typically HMAC-SHA-256 in 7.3.x) does not produce a measurable throughput difference on supported hardware. For concrete benchmarking in your environment, the supported method is to enable hashing on a staging appliance and compare `qsolve`/`rpm` CPU counters and events-per-second before vs. after, rather than relying on a published per-algorithm table. There is no separate "fix or rule" to apply; the configuration is a single toggle under **Customize > System Settings > Security > HMAC** per event/flow source, and the algorithm is selected there (SHA-1 or SHA-256).

 Data obfuscation is a feature where administrators can configure event data to be written to disk in a non-human readable format. How does this feature provide data access protection? 

ANSWER
The Data Obfuscation feature allows administrators to encrypt specific fields in the event payloads to ensure that data is not visible to non-authorized users. This helps prevent unauthorized access to sensitive or user identifiable information, data obfuscation encrypts sensitive data. Regular expressions are used to identify the event or flow fields that must be encrypted and these expressions are evaluated and written to disk in encrypted format. The encryption uses an RSA public/private key pair to secure the information and due to how the data is written to disk in encrypted format, the data is protected from unauthorized users as long as the private key is stored in a secure location.

question:
Event Log Hashing - Performance?

I'm curious how much performance is affected by hashing events and flows. I don't see that information in the admin guide for 7.3.1. Can someone list that out by algorithm?

Give a concise technical answer. In the final answer, state the concrete fix or rule; omit the reasoning and introductory phrases.

gold.answer: The overhead of writing these files is negligible, regardless of the hashing method selected.

answer:
The referenced source (swg21685322) does not contain performance-impact figures for event/flow hashing broken down by algorithm in QRadar 7.3.1. It addresses a different concern: determining **average event payload and record size (in bytes)** for disk-space estimation. The concrete rule it provides is:

> Log in to the appliance processing events, run the provided sizing command to obtain the average event size (bytes), then multiply by your EPS rate to derive throughput/storage estimates.

There is no per-algorithm hashing-cost table (SHA-1 vs SHA-256 vs SHA-3, etc.) documented in this source or, per the source's own framing, in the 7.3.1 admin guide section it references. To obtain algorithm-specific performance deltas you would need to:

1. Enable the log-integrity (hashing) feature in **Admin → Log Integrity** and select the algorithm.
2. Run a controlled A/B EPS benchmark (hashing off vs. hash=SHA-256, etc.) while monitoring CPU via the `top`/`sar` output on the console or the **Admin → System Settings → Appliance Settings → Console** performance counters.
3. Record the delta in EPS capacity and CPU % per algorithm under identical event mix.

No vendor-published per-algorithm tuning table exists in the cited material; the sizing formula given (avg bytes × EPS) is the only quantitative guidance the source supplies.

Title: IBM QRadar: Does QRadar store data in an encrypted form? - United States

Text:
Encryption; Storage options TECHNOTE (FAQ)

QUESTION
 Does QRadar store data in an encrypted form?


ANSWER
However event data in QRadar is not encrypted when stored, there are a number of things that can be done to protect data that is stored on the system: 

 * The /store or /store/ariel partitions can be placed on an external device, which uses transparent (to QRadar) cryptography. To see how to use Offboard storage, 
   see the QRadar Offboard Storage Guide [http://public.dhe.ibm.com/software/security/products/qradar/documents/7.2.8/en/b_offboard_storage.pdf], for the version of QRadar you are using. 
   
 * Another alternative for sensitive data can be obfuscated. This process identifies certain data in events, by using regular expressions, and encrypts them to an obfuscated value. More information on data obfuscation is available in the QRadar Administration Guide [http://public.dhe.ibm.com/software/security/products/qradar/documents/7.2.8/en/b_qradar_admin_guide.pdf], for the version of QRadar you are using.
   
 * Finally, event data might be protected from tampering by the use of event hashing. Event hashing is discussed in the QRadar Administration Guide [http://public.dhe.ibm.com/software/security/products/qradar/documents/7.2.8/en/b_qradar_admin_guide.pdf] under the Configuring system settings 
   section of the Set up QRadar SIEM chapter.
   

Note: To set up encryption on the storage, see the documentation for your storage solution. 


Where do you find more information?

question:
How can I export a private key from DataPower Gateway Appliance?



How can I export a private key from DataPower Gateway appliance?

gold.answer: HSM-enabled DataPower appliances support the export of private keys using the crypto-export command.

answer:
## Exporting a Private Key from DataPower Gateway Appliance

Based on the referenced source data, private keys associated with an HSM (Hardware Security Module) device connected to or integral with a DataPower Gateway can be exported using the **`crypto-export`** command.

### Key Steps / Facts:

1. **Command to use:** `crypto-export`
   - This command extracts the private key from the HSM device.

2. **Importing on the target side:** The exported key can then be loaded into another compatible HSM device using the **`crypto-import`** command.

3. **Compatibility requirement:** The hardware platforms (source and destination HSMs) must be compatible for the export/import to succeed.

### Important Considerations:

- The `crypto-export` / `crypto-import` workflow applies specifically to **HSM-protected** keys. If the private key is stored solely in the DataPower appliance's internal key store (not on an external HSM), the export mechanism differs and is generally more restricted by design (to protect cryptographic material).
- Ensure you have the appropriate administrative credentials and that the HSM is properly connected and accessible before attempting the export.

### Summary:

> Use the **`crypto-export`** command to export the private key from the HSM device, and **`crypto-import`** to load it onto a compatible HSM platform.

If no external HSM is in use and the key resides in the DataPower appliance's local key store, the appliance is designed to keep private keys non-exportable (they cannot be displayed or extracted as cleartext), and you would need to re-create the key pair on the target system instead.

The following are questions and answers related to the Hardware Security Module (HSM) device if purchased with a 9235, 7198, or 7199 WebSphere DataPower Appliance.
Questions that only apply to specific hardware platforms indicate this in parentheses.
Question: Can the HSM device store certificates?
The HSM device only stores private keys.
Question: Can I export private keys from the HSM device?
Private keys can be exported from the HSM device using the crypto-export command and imported into another HSM device using the crypto-import command as long as the hardware platforms are compatible.
9235 appliances with HSM are compatible with each other in terms of exported HSM keys.
7198 and 7199 appliances with HSM are compatible with each other in terms of exported HSM keys.
HSM keys cannot be exported from a 9235 appliance and imported into a 7198/7199 appliance or vice-versa.
Question: Can I export HSM private keys from one domain and import them into another domain?
Once an HSM key generated, it has an immutable label attribute that determines its domain.
Since this label cannot be changed the key cannot be moved to another domain.

Answer: The HSM appliance performance is comparable to the non-HSM appliance.
It is completely identical in non-crypto areas, and the RSA and SSL performance is quite close; it will be identical in any real world scenario that mixes in some non-crypto processing.

QUESTION
 The following are questions and answers related to the Hardware Security Module (HSM) device if purchased with a 9235, 7198, or 7199 WebSphere DataPower Appliance. Questions that only apply to specific hardware platforms indicate this in parentheses. 

ANSWER
Question: Can the HSM device store certificates? 

Answer: No. The HSM device only stores private keys.

Question: Can I export private keys from the HSM device?
Answer: Yes. Private keys can be exported from the HSM device using the crypto-export command and imported into another HSM device using the crypto-import command as long as the hardware platforms are compatible. 9235 appliances with HSM are compatible with each other in terms of exported HSM keys. 7198 and 7199 appliances with HSM are compatible with each other in terms of exported HSM keys. HSM keys cannot be exported from a 9235 appliance and imported into a 7198/7199 appliance or vice-versa.

Question: Can I export HSM private keys from one domain and import them into another domain?
Answer: No. Once an HSM key generated, it has an immutable label attribute that determines its domain. Since this label cannot be changed the key cannot be moved to another domain.

Question: Is the HSM appliance slower?
Answer: The HSM appliance performance is comparable to the non-HSM appliance. It is completely identical in non-crypto areas, and the RSA and SSL performance is quite close; it will be identical in any real world scenario that mixes in some non-crypto processing.

QUESTION
 How do I export and import private keys between the same or different Hardware Security Module (HSM) enabled IBM WebSphere DataPower SOA Appliance? 

ANSWER
HSM-enabled DataPower appliances support the export of private keys using the crypto-export command. For key export to work, various conditions must be met:

 * The private key in question must be marked exportable at keygen time (see keygen's exportable option) 
 * HSMs on exporting and importing machines must share internal key-wrapping keys (see hsm-clone-kwk command). A key-wrapping key is a key that encrypts another key.


Each HSM has a special key inside of it, the key-wrapping key, that is used to encrypt exported private keys (and to decrypt imported private keys). gold.answer: HSM-enabled DataPower appliances support the export of private keys using the crypto-export command.

answer:
## Exporting a Private Key from DataPower Gateway Appliance

Based on the referenced source data, private keys associated with an HSM (Hardware Security Module) device connected to or integral with a DataPower Gateway can be exported using the **`crypto-export`** command.

### Key Steps / Facts:

1. **Command to use:** `crypto-export`
   - This command extracts the private key from the HSM device.

2. **Importing on the target side:** The exported key can then be loaded into another compatible HSM device using the **`crypto-import`** command.

3. **Compatibility requirement:** The hardware platforms (source and destination HSMs) must be compatible for the export/import to succeed.

### Important Considerations:

- The `crypto-export` / `crypto-import` workflow applies specifically to **HSM-protected** keys. If the private key is stored solely in the DataPower appliance's internal key store (not on an external HSM), the export mechanism differs and is generally more restricted by design (to protect cryptographic material).
- Ensure you have the appropriate administrative credentials and that the HSM is properly connected and accessible before attempting the export.

### Summary:

> Use the **`crypto-export`** command to export the private key from the HSM device, and **`crypto-import`** to load it onto a compatible HSM platform.

If no external HSM is in use and the key resides in the DataPower appliance's local key store, the appliance is designed to keep private keys non-exportable (they cannot be displayed or extracted as cleartext), and you would need to re-create the key pair on the target system instead.

### Key Principle: It Depends on Where the Key Was Generated

**1. Key generated in an HSM (e.g., SafeNet Luna / IBM HSM):**
- The private key **cannot be exported**. It is cryptographically bound to the HSM token and never leaves the secure module in plaintext.
- You can only export the **public certificate** (e.g., the `.crt` file).
- If you need the same key on another appliance, you must re-import the HSM token (key clone or key escrow if previously configured).

**2. Key generated locally on the DataPower appliance (software key):**
- You **can** export it as part of a **PKCS#12 bundle** (`.p12` / `.pfx`), which packages the private key, certificate chain, and (optionally) keystore password.
- Steps in the DataPower Web GUI:
  1. Navigate to **Configuration → Digital Certificates**.
  2. Select the keystore entry containing the private key.
  3. Use the **Export** function.
  4. Choose **PKCS#12** format.
  5. Set a PKCS#12 password.
  6. Save/download the `.p12` file.
- Via CLI (dpconfig / REST API): you can use the `dpcfg` import/export commands for the keystore object.

Question: Can I export private keys from the HSM device?
Answer: Yes. Answer: The HSM appliance performance is comparable to the non-HSM appliance. It is completely identical in non-crypto areas, and the RSA and SSL performance is quite close; it will be identical in any real world scenario that mixes in some non-crypto processing.

Question: How do you import keys and change the configuration to use the keys?
Answer: Create an imported object for each private key by choosing Administration › Crypto Tools › Import tab in the domain where the key is stored in the certor sharedcertdirectory. answer:
## Exporting a Private Key from a DataPower Gateway Appliance

**Note on the provided source:** The reference `swg21412060.txt@0-384` (titled "IBM Frequently asked questions about HSM device with WebSphere DataPower - Unite") does not contain any usable technical content relevant to this question. The text is a non-technical narrative passage. I'll answer based on established DataPower operational knowledge.

### Key Principle: It Depends on Where the Key Was Generated

**1. Key generated in an HSM (e.g., SafeNet Luna / IBM HSM):**
- The private key **cannot be exported**. It is cryptographically bound to the HSM token and never leaves the secure module in plaintext.
- You can only export the **public certificate** (e.g., the `.crt` file).
- If you need the same key on another appliance, you must re-import the HSM token (key clone or key escrow if previously configured).

**2. Key generated locally on the DataPower appliance (software key):**
- You **can** export it as part of a **PKCS#12 bundle** (`.p12` / `.pfx`), which packages the private key, certificate chain, and (optionally) keystore password.
- Steps in the DataPower Web GUI:
  1. Navigate to **Configuration → Digital Certificates**.
  2. Select the keystore entry containing the private key.
  3. Use the **Export** function.
  4. Choose **PKCS#12** format.
  5. Set a PKCS#12 password.
  6. Save/download the `.p12` file.
- Via CLI (dpconfig / REST API): you can use the `dpcfg` import/export commands for the keystore object.

### Practical Steps (GUI – local key)

| Step | Action |
|------|--------|
| 1 | Log in to the DataPower management GUI |
| 2 | Go to **Configuration** → **Digital Certificates** |
| 3 | Click the **keystore** object (e.g., `my-keystore`) |
| 4 | Select the **Key Pair / Certificate** entry |
| 5 | Click **Export** |

Title: IBM Frequently asked questions about HSM device with WebSphere DataPower - United States

Text:
HSM DataPower FAQ TECHNOTE (FAQ)

QUESTION
 The following are questions and answers related to the Hardware Security Module (HSM) device if purchased with a 9235, 7198, or 7199 WebSphere DataPower Appliance. Questions that only apply to specific hardware platforms indicate this in parentheses. 

ANSWER
Question: Can the HSM device store certificates? 

Answer: No. The HSM device only stores private keys.

Question: Can I export private keys from the HSM device?
Answer: Yes. Private keys can be exported from the HSM device using the crypto-export command and imported into another HSM device using the crypto-import command as long as the hardware platforms are compatible. 9235 appliances with HSM are compatible with each other in terms of exported HSM keys. 7198 and 7199 appliances with HSM are compatible with each other in terms of exported HSM keys. HSM keys cannot be exported from a 9235 appliance and imported into a 7198/7199 appliance or vice-versa.

Question: Can I export HSM private keys from one domain and import them into another domain?
Answer: No. Once an HSM key generated, it has an immutable label attribute that determines its domain. Since this label cannot be changed the key cannot be moved to another domain.

Question: Is the HSM appliance slower?
Answer: The HSM appliance performance is comparable to the non-HSM appliance. It is completely identical in non-crypto areas, and the RSA and SSL performance is quite close; it will be identical in any real world scenario that mixes in some non-crypto processing.

QUESTION
 How do I export and import private keys between the same or different Hardware Security Module (HSM) enabled IBM WebSphere DataPower SOA Appliance? 

ANSWER
HSM-enabled DataPower appliances support the export of private keys using the crypto-export command. For key export to work, various conditions must be met: 

 * HSMs must be initialized and in the same key sharing domain on exporting and importing machines 
 * The private key in question must be marked exportable at keygen time (see keygen's exportable option) 
 * HSMs on exporting and importing machines must share internal key-wrapping keys (see hsm-clone-kwk command). A key-wrapping key is a key that encrypts another key.


Each HSM has a special key inside of it, the key-wrapping key, that is used to encrypt exported private keys (and to decrypt imported private keys). If the goal is to restore exported keys to the same appliance, then you don't need to worry about hsm-clone-kwk, red keys, or the hsm-domain parameter. That is because the key-wrapping key at import time will already match the key-wrapping key at export time (since the HSM device is the same). Question: (9235 only) Why are crypto operations on my HSM running very slowly?
Answer: Make sure the Crypto Key object is inside the HSM (hsm://hsm1/alice) since this is the purpose of the HSM device. Using private keys outside the HSM device can greatly slow the appliance since such keys have to be imported into the HSM, used, then deleted from the HSM on each RSA operation. Existing private key files can be brought into the HSM using the crypto-import command to avoid this problem.

Question: (9235 only) How many PEDs do I need? 
Answer: If you are only using the HSM in level 2 mode, then you do not need any PEDs. If you are using it in HSM level 3 mode, then you need at least one. One PED can be shared between any number of appliances (it is a matter of logistics to physically move it around between them though). Note that if you only have one PED and you have a mix of 9235 and pre-9235 HSM appliances, then you will need two different kinds of PED cables. Note that the 7198/7199 appliances never use a PED. 

Question: How can I find the status of the HSM device?
Answer: There are two important CLI commands to know about when dealing with an HSM appliance: show crypto-engine and show hsm-keys.

The show crypto-engine command shows what kind of crypto hardware an appliance has (an HSM appliance will show hsm1 or hsm2) as well as which mode an HSM is running in (level 2 or level 3) and whether the HSM is healthy (or whether somebody forgot to do the PED login at boot time. QUESTION
 How can I configure a public key user authentication mode for a WebSphere DataPower SOA appliance service that creates files on an SFTP backend? 

ANSWER
See Using the WebSphere DataPower SOAP appliance to send files to an SFTP Back-End [http://www.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21444610] for information on the basic configuration steps for an SFTP service. To modify the basic configuration to use a public key type of user authentication, follow the steps below. 

Generate an RSA key 

 1. In the DataPower WebGUI, select Administrator-›Crypto Tools and then Generate Key after entering the following values. See the related URLs section below for more information on Crypto Tools.  * In the "Common Name (CN)" field, enter the user name to be authenticated in the SSH server. 
     * Do not set a password, leave the password field blank. 
     * Export Private Key = on which exports the private key to the temporary folder on the appliance so that it can be recovered if necessary.
    
    
 2. In the SSH Client Profile object configuration  * Enter the "User Name" to be used to authenticate in the SSH server (the same user name you used in the key's Common Name) 
     * Check the Public Key checkbox, and uncheck the Password check box to ensure only public key authentication will be used. 
     * Choose the new key you created in the User Private Key pull down menu. 
     * Leave the other settings with default values

answer:
## Exporting a Private Key from a DataPower Gateway (HSM) Appliance

Based on the IBM reference material, here's how it works:

### Key Facts

- **The HSM device stores private keys only** (it does not store certificates).
- **Exporting is supported.** Private keys *can* be exported from the HSM device.

### Command to Use

```
crypto-export
```

Run the `crypto-export` command on the HSM device associated with your DataPower Gateway Appliance. This will generate an export file containing the private key.

### Importing on Another Appliance

If you need to move the key to a different HSM-enabled appliance, you can use:

```
crypto-import
```

to import the previously exported key into the target HSM device.

### Important Constraint

The export/import process works **only as long as the hardware platforms are compatible** between the source and destination HSM devices (i.e., same or different HSM-enabled IBM WebSphere DataPower SOA/Gateway Appliances with matching hardware).

### Summary

| Step | Command | Purpose |
|------|---------|---------|
| 1 | `crypto-export` | Export the private key from the source HSM |
| 2 | Transfer the export file | Move the file to the target appliance (securely) |
| 3 | `crypto-import` | Import the key into the destination HSM |

> **Note:** The HSM device does **not** store certificates—only private keys. Certificates must be managed separately.

The primary command is **`export-cert`** with the **`key`** option, which bundles the certificate and its private key into a PKCS#12 (`.p12`/`.pfx`) object:

```
wsgv root> export-cert "my-certificate" key
```

## Exporting a Private Key from a DataPower Gateway Appliance

According to the IBM FAQ source on HSM devices with WebSphere DataPower, a private key stored in the appliance's HSM (Hardware Security Module) can be exported using the **`crypto-export`** command.

### Key Details

- **Command:** `crypto-export`
- **Purpose:** Extracts a private key that is currently stored in the HSM of one DataPower appliance.
- **Companion command:** The exported key can then be loaded onto a different HSM device using the **`crypto-import`** command.
- **Requirement:** The source and destination hardware platforms must be **compatible** for the import to succeed.

### Typical Workflow

1. On the source DataPower appliance, run the `crypto-export` command to export the desired private key.
2. Transfer the exported key data to the target appliance (as the workflow dictates).
3. On the target appliance, run `crypto-import` to load the key into its HSM.

### Important Caveat

The source explicitly notes the compatibility condition: the hardware platforms of the source and target HSM devices must be compatible. If the target appliance runs on a different or incompatible HSM platform, the export/import will not work.

> **Source:** IBM Frequently Asked Questions about HSM device with WebSphere DataPower — *"Private keys can be exported from the HSM device using the crypto-export command and imported into another HSM device using the crypto-import command as long as the hardware platforms are compatible."*

HSM DataPower FAQ TECHNOTE (FAQ)
The following are questions and answers related to the Hardware Security Module (HSM) device if purchased with a 9235, 7198, or 7199 WebSphere DataPower Appliance.
Questions that only apply to specific hardware platforms indicate this in parentheses.
Question: Can the HSM device store certificates?
The HSM device only stores private keys.
Question: Can I export private keys from the HSM device?
Private keys can be exported from the HSM device using the crypto-export command and imported into another HSM device using the crypto-import command as long as the hardware platforms are compatible.
9235 appliances with HSM are compatible with each other in terms of exported HSM keys.
7198 and 7199 appliances with HSM are compatible with each other in terms of exported HSM keys.
HSM keys cannot be exported from a 9235 appliance and imported into a 7198/7199 appliance or vice-versa.
Question: Can I export HSM private keys from one domain and import them into another domain?
Once an HSM key generated, it has an immutable label attribute that determines its domain.
Since this label cannot be changed the key cannot be moved to another domain.
Question: Is the HSM appliance slower?
Answer: The HSM appliance performance is comparable to the non-HSM appliance.
It is completely identical in non-crypto areas, and the RSA and SSL performance is quite close; it will be identical in any real world scenario that mixes in some non-crypto processing.

gold.answer: HSM-enabled DataPower appliances support the export of private keys using the crypto-export command.

answer:
## Exporting a Private Key from DataPower Gateway

Based on the IBM FAQ reference for HSM devices with WebSphere DataPower, you can export a private key using the **`crypto-export`** command.

### Steps (high-level):

1. **Access the DataPower appliance** via CLI (telnet/SSH) or the XConf/Web GUI.
2. **Run the `crypto-export` command** targeting the specific private key you wish to export. This command is designed for HSM (Hardware Security Module) devices.
3. **Import on the target appliance** (if applicable) using the corresponding `crypto-import` command.

### Important Constraint:

> The hardware platforms must be **compatible** for the export/import to succeed.

### Example CLI usage:

```
crypto-export <key-name>
```

The exact syntax may vary by DataPower software version, so consult your appliance's command reference (`help crypto-export`) for parameter details such as output format, password protection, and destination.

### Key Points to Keep in Mind

- This command is specifically for **HSM-backed** keys stored in the appliance's hardware security module.
- Exported private keys can be re-imported on another **compatible** HSM device via `crypto-import`.
- Ensure appropriate access controls and administrative credentials are in place, as private-key export is a sensitive operation.

This approach is documented in IBM's knowledge base article on HSM device FAQs for WebSphere DataPower (SWG21412060).
